All of that combined will make your presentation shine and stand out. - David Strausser, Fonseca Advisers
8. Tap Into The International Market
Today, AI enables local businesses to enter the international market without facing traditional barriers. Language, cultural and social questions can all be addressed by artificial intelligence. AI can also be used to tailor marketing materials, understand regional business nuances and communicate in languages that might be unfamiliar to you. As a result, your business will gain credibility. - Dima Raketa, Reputation House
9. Validate Decisions By Verifying Rationale
AI is now a common, open resource for leaders. When building a convincing argument regarding a controversial decision, having a strong supporting rationale is quite important. Using GPT resources to verify and validate each party’s resources throughout the conversation can allow you to focus on debating the value of ideas rather than preparing documentation. - Gyehyon Andrea Jo, MVLASF
10. Speed Up Market And Customer Research
AI is a game-changer for leaders when it comes to all things related to serving customers. Product or service quality and a quick time to market are critical when it comes to building credibility in the marketplace. Artificial intelligence tools can enable leaders to more quickly conduct market and customer research; assemble customer success stories and testimonials; build compelling storyboards, pitches and investor relations materials; and more. - Archana Rao, Innova Solutions
11. Recommend Products Based On Customers’ Needs
Leaders can boost their company’s credibility with AI-driven product recommendations. By demonstrating a deep understanding of consumer needs, leaders can increase sales, foster customer loyalty and build a reputation for innovation. Integrating AI-powered insights into marketing strategies and customer-engagement initiatives further boosts the company’s image as a customer-centric organization. - Gunjan Paliwal, Meta

title: Council Post: How To Maximize (And Minimize) Technology To Boost Sustainability
text:
When it comes to sustainability, technology can be a double-edged sword. While there are digital solutions that can help companies streamline operations and minimize their carbon footprints, it’s also true that heavy use of technology can consume large amounts of energy.
Balancing leveraging technology solutions for more sustainable operations with managing how (and how much) they lean on energy-consuming digital tools and processes can be a complicated challenge for organizations across industries. Below, members of Forbes Technology Council discuss smart ways companies can maximize (and minimize) their tech usage to boost sustainability and shrink their environmental impact.
1. Leverage Online Collaboration Platforms
Leveraging online collaboration platforms reduces business travel. Less time spent driving and flying will reduce the carbon emissions that contribute to climate change. Access to high-speed, low-latency, ubiquitous broadband connectivity is key to successful use of online collaborative platforms. Leaders concerned about sustainability should prioritize these tools when planning their annual operating strategies. - Glenn Katz, Telesat
2. Embrace Network Technologies
Nowadays, network technologies help businesses to not only sustain their operations, but also to scale. For example, Netflix would have remained solely a DVD rental company if it hadn’t embraced the rise of internet technology. Over the past 70 years, network technologies have undergone revolutionary changes, and it is essential for companies to keep pace with them. - Alexander Britkin, NFWare
Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?
3. Optimize Resource Use Via Advanced Data Analytics
One practical way organizations can leverage technology for sustainability is by implementing advanced data analytics and artificial intelligence to optimize resource use. These technologies can significantly reduce waste and energy consumption by predicting demand and enhancing efficiency across operations. - Savitri Sagar, Kenzo Infotech
4. Digitize Core Operations
To achieve sustainability goals, companies need to look at the indirect benefits of digitizing their core operations. For example, digitizing the mortgage process doesn’t just save paper, but also avoids everyone needing to travel to come to the closing table. How do your operations impact your employees and customers? You’ll find that providing a better, digital experience often leads to a lower environmental impact. - Pat Kinsel, Proof (fka Notarize)
5. Reimagine The Design, Manufacture And Disposal Of Products
Look inward to reimagine how to design, manufacture and dispose of products, ensuring you minimize the environmental impact of each step. Technology that shows all aspects of the supply chain provides a clear view into operations. With a line of sight into product development, sustainable processes can easily be tracked, providing a complete understanding and enabling you to meet consumer expectations related to sustainability. - Ross Meyercord, Propel Software
6. Set Up Systems To Track Environmental Data
One of the most critical aspects of accelerating sustainability progress and goals is the ability to track, analyze and report reliable environmental data quickly. Knowing this, we implemented Salesforce’s Net Zero Cloud with Workiva’s reporting platform to help us make better, data-driven decisions as we decarbonize our operations and work to achieve a 55% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2035. - Daragh Mahon, Werner Enterprises
7. Adopt A Digital-First Approach
I love the smell of books and the feeling of paper in my hands, but to be an ecologically responsible company, adopt a digital-first approach. Think twice before printing reports if they can be viewed interactively online. Evaluate if one-time use printouts are necessary, and use AI to create digital notes for you instead of going through reams of notebooks. - Teri Thomas, Volpara Health
8. Explore Local Production Options
There are three dimensions of sustainability: environmental, social and governance. Companies must address all three. Environmental aspects, such as CO2 emissions, get a lot of attention, but social and governance factors are equally vital. Local production positively impacts all three dimensions. It reduces transport distances, empowers creators globally while producing locally, and ensures production meets strict codes of conduct. - Henrik Müller-Hansen, Gelato
9. Use AI Predictive Maintenance Tools
Utility operators have seen an immediate improvement from simple AI applications, such as using AI to determine which trees are most at risk of bringing down power lines (the No. 1 cause of outages). AI can predict which equipment is about to fail so operators can take steps before it does. It can also create more accurate underground maps so operators can avoid costly missteps when expanding energy networks. - Steve Smith, National Grid Partners
10. Focus On Operational Efficiency
A focus on operational efficiency is the first practical step on the journey to meeting sustainability goals. Aspects include continuous monitoring to adapt to business conditions and opportunities, utilization of AI-based automation to optimize asset-intensive processes, and leveraging generative AI for guidance on the right pathways to achieve long-term sustainability goals. - Heiko Claussen, Aspen Technology, Inc.
11. Test Designs Via Digital Twin Technology
Much of a company’s impact comes from the products it makes, pointing to the importance of sustainable design and raw materials. Digital twin technology allows organizations to test design decisions via a virtual replica, which not only reduces the time between iterations, but also eliminates the need for physical prototypes, saving materials and production resources to further sustainability goals. - Neil D’Souza, Makersite
12. Optimize Energy Usage Through Internet Of Things Devices
One practical way to boost sustainability is implementing IoT-based energy management systems. These systems use sensors and smart meters to monitor and optimize energy consumption in real time, reducing waste and improving efficiency. By identifying patterns and areas of high usage, organizations can make informed decisions to reduce their carbon footprints and lower their energy costs. - Hadi Tabani, Liquid Technologies
13. Implement Asset Performance Management Principles
Organizations can leverage technology to meet sustainability goals by implementing rigorous asset performance management principles and data-driven frameworks. When implemented, they optimize asset production and minimize waste and costs, leading to greater efficiency, sustainability and ROI. - Alexander Clausbruch, Radix
14. Leverage Energy-Efficient Data Centers And Cloud Services
Organizations can improve sustainability by implementing energy-efficient data centers and cloud services. For instance, using AI-driven optimization strategies to manage server loads and cooling systems can greatly decrease power consumption. We’ve seen tech leaders cut energy usage in their data centers in half, which demonstrates how tech innovations can drive substantial environmental benefits. - Ivan Guzenko, SmartyAds Inc.
15. Reduce The Need For New Devices Through Virtualization
Virtualization allows the efficient use of existing hardware, reducing the need for new devices. This not only helps companies cut costs, but also minimizes the environmental impact of manufacturing. By running multiple operating systems on a single device, virtualization eliminates the need for multiple devices, promoting eco-friendly practices. - Prashant Ketkar, Parallels (part of Alludo)
16. Tap Into The Expertise Of Specialists
To meet sustainability goals, organizations should calculate their carbon footprints by working with specialized tech providers to identify key improvement areas. Additionally, exploring audited carbon-offset programs can enhance sustainability strategies, particularly for financial institutions aiming to meet ESG goals. - Karan Jain, NayaOne
17. Look At New Tech Investments Through A Sustainability Lens
Sustainability has expanded to include not just environmental goals, but also larger goals around business continuity and longevity. Reconsider what fits into that new definition, and apply that focus to your tech investments, maintaining the integrity of critical challenges related to supply chain optimization, talent retention and recruitment, and boosting employee productivity and impact. - Ed Jennings, Quickbase

title: How Huawei Is Rivaling Nvidia In GenAI
text:

While U.S. companies like OpenAI, Nvidia and Google lead the charge, and China boasts contenders such as Baidu and Alibaba, another heavyweight is making significant strides: Huawei. - Ecosystem collaboration is another crucial element, as partnerships can accelerate AI adoption and innovation, providing customized solutions for specific industries.
- Additionally, staying ahead of geopolitical and regulatory challenges is essential, as these can significantly impact AI deployment and market leadership.

Huawei's Pangu Model 5.0 excels in handling tasks across text, images, videos, and audio, adapting to various languages and scenarios. Its ability to revolutionize industrial design, significantly shortening the design process for new vehicles, illustrates its transformative potential across industries. The Soul: HarmonyOS NEXT

Addressing key challenges in large language model training—such as the "computing wall," "memory wall," and "energy efficiency wall"—Huawei has launched the Elastic Memory Storage Service, leveraging its patented Memory Pooling technology to overcome these barriers. Huawei's GenAI strategy exemplifies its ambition to lead in this transformative field. Its comprehensive efforts—from foundational AI computing power, exemplified by the Ascend 910C chip, to innovative applications—are positioning it as a global frontrunner. For senior executives, the lessons from Huawei's approach underscore the critical importance of full-stack innovation, strategic collaboration, and long-term vision in securing a leadership position in the rapidly evolving AI landscape.

title: The New Data Economy: What Your Business Should Know
text:
We all know that Artificial Intelligence (AI) is here. We further know that AI relies on data. Businesses are increasingly becoming aware of the need for good data literacy and good data practices, sometimes as a precursor to, and sometimes as a critical partner element to, a good AI strategy. However, the landscape of data is also changing.
Why Does Data Matter to AI
AI, as a technology, builds everything by learning patterns from data. The past decade has seen dramatic improvements in AI partly because of the perfect storm of massive datasets meeting powerful computational hardware. While the data required to build effective AI depends very much on the problem domain, it is generally understood that larger datasets enable more options for powerful AIs. As the world realizes the importance of AI capabilities to national, regional and corporate competitiveness, who has access to what data becomes a key part of this competitiveness.
Where Does Data Come From?
Historically, data came from past experiences. For example, a bank may have data about the last decade of their customers. A hospital may have patient records. In these scenarios, data literacy and data management came down to making sure the data that an organization had access to was protected, well managed, and effectively used. These days however, an organization’s internal data is only one lever that is available in the story.
Data Augmentation and Synthetic Data
Technology advances have made it possible to augment existing data (generate new data programmatically), use synthetic data from simulations and other sources, or simply use AI techniques that are less data reliant. Depending on your domain, one or more of these methods can become a key part of a data strategy.
Foundational Models and Transfer Methods
Another powerful capability of AI is the ability to build one AI on another, using methods like fine-tuning or transfer learning. A class of AIs, called Foundation Models, are emblematic of this trend. These models have been trained with often massive datasets, but can be used in applications without necessarily having access to the original training data, and tuned for a range of purposes that leverage the understanding of the underlying dataset.
Open Data
As countries recognize the criticality of data to AI competitiveness, there are fears that an AI race will include a data race. To drive more equitable access to AI, organizations are creating public data repositories, in areas ranging from medicine (see an example of the Cancer Imaging Archive) to public repositories to train Generative AI models comprising trillions of text tokens and billions of images.
Data Marketplaces
Finally, it is also possible to buy and sell data in data marketplaces. This is particularly interesting since it directly connects to the value of data by putting a price on it. In some industries, custom datasets can also be curated, labeled, and purchased from companies that specialize in data generation.
Takeaways for Your Business
What does this mean for your business? It means that a data strategy is critical to any business looking to benefit from AI, and that while a data strategy should always include careful management of internal data, it is no longer limited to this element. A comprehensive data strategy for a business should now include understanding what public data sources may be relevant, what foundational models can bring in digested insights, what synthetic data and augmentation can be used, and what data if any can be purchased. By combining these elements, it is possible to create a powerful data strategy that can then enable Return on Investment (ROI) from AI solutions.

title: Company that sent AI calls mimicking Joe Biden to New Hampshire voters agrees to pay $1 million fine
text:
Company that sent AI calls mimicking Joe Biden to New Hampshire voters agrees to pay $1 million fine
A company that sent deceptive calls to New Hampshire voters using artificial intelligence to mimic President Joe Biden’s voice has agreed to pay a $1 million fine, federal regulators said
MEREDITH, N.H. -- A company that sent deceptive calls to New Hampshire voters using artificial intelligence to mimic President Joe Biden’s voice agreed Wednesday to pay a $1 million fine, federal regulators said.
Lingo Telecom, the voice service provider that transmitted the robocalls, agreed to the settlement to resolve enforcement action taken by the Federal Communications Commission, which had initially sought a $2 million fine.
The case is seen by many as an unsettling early example of how AI might be used to influence groups of voters and democracy as a whole.
Meanwhile Steve Kramer, a political consultant who orchestrated the calls, still faces a proposed $6 million FCC fine as well as state criminal charges.
The phone messages were sent to thousands of New Hampshire voters on Jan. 21. They featured a voice similar to Biden’s falsely suggesting that voting in the state’s presidential primary would preclude them from casting ballots in the November general election.
Kramer, who paid a magician and self-described “digital nomad” to create the recording, told The Associated Press earlier this year that he wasn't trying to influence the outcome of the primary, but he rather wanted to highlight the potential dangers of AI and spur lawmakers into action.
If found guilty, Kramer could face a prison sentence of up to seven years on a charge of voter suppression and a sentence of up to one year on a charge of impersonating a candidate.
The FCC said that as well as agreeing to the civil fine, Lingo Telecom had agreed to strict caller ID authentication rules and requirements and to more thoroughly verify the accuracy of the information provided by its customers and upstream providers.
“Every one of us deserves to know that the voice on the line is exactly who they claim to be,” FCC chairperson Jessica Rosenworcel said in a statement. “If AI is being used, that should be made clear to any consumer, citizen, and voter who encounters it. The FCC will act when trust in our communications networks is on the line.”
Lingo Telecom did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The company had earlier said it strongly disagreed with the FCC’s action, calling it an attempt to impose new rules retroactively.
Nonprofit consumer advocacy group Public Citizen commended the FCC on its action. Co-president Robert Weissman said Rosenworcel got it “exactly right” by saying consumers have a right to know when they are receiving authentic content and when they are receiving AI-generated deepfakes. Weissman said the case illustrates how such deepfakes pose “an existential threat to our democracy.”
FCC Enforcement Bureau Chief Loyaan Egal said the combination of caller ID spoofing and generative AI voice-cloning technology posed a significant threat “whether at the hands of domestic operatives seeking political advantage or sophisticated foreign adversaries conducting malign influence or election interference activities."

title: Is AI Coming For Coders’ Jobs? It’s Much More Interesting Than That
text:
Is AI going to eliminate a lot of developers’ jobs? There is a gulf between developers and the general population when it comes to answering that question.
If you were to ask developers if they think their jobs are in danger in the near term, most of them will quickly tell you that there is no imminent threat. In fact, according to Atlassian’s latest State of Developer Experience Report, 62% of developers think that today’s AI either doesn’t improve their productivity or improves it only slightly. So, while we are seeing some great new AI technology out there, the industry is still working towards broader adoption and more useful developer-oriented capabilities.
However, among the general public there is a misconception that developer jobs are a prime target for AI replacement. I can understand this perception when anyone can go to an AI website, ask for some code and it just comes back to you. But after looking deeper at current and future product roadmaps for major software vendors, I have reached two conclusions. First, developers will continue to be valued resources for some time to come—years, at least. Second, we are entering a second generation of developer-assistance technologies that greatly enhance developer jobs—without threatening to replace them.
Human Developers Will Remain Valued For Some Time To Come
Why do I say this? Because of all the ground that developers must cover in doing their work, and the limitations of any AI tool or set of tools that would try to cover that ground. Three major factors stand out to me.
- Developers do a lot more than writing code — When you try to foresee the jobs that may be in danger of becoming obsolete in the age of AI, you need to consider two things. First, the role has to be somewhat static and repeatable such that the benefits from AI can kick in at scale. This is why we hear so much about AI in the context of customer service: the workflows are pretty static in the majority of cases, there are relatively few exceptions that need to be handled by humans and bots can work 24/7. Second, any job that requires genuine creativity will not do well with current generative AI or machine learning models. In today’s AI, the goal is to find the best answer based upon many sources of generalized knowledge. Yet creativity and innovation are not generally born of commonly held information. Both of these qualifiers protect developers as a target for AI replacement. Devs live in a very dynamic job space marked by constant change, lots of ambiguity and high creative requirements. So, sure, AI can help developers. But in the absence of some new type of AI we haven’t seen yet, current AI tools would make poor developers on their own.
- Today’s AI can help, if you know how to drive it — Prompt-based assistants perform relatively simple tasks very quickly based on human-generated requests. But, to get more advanced, you may require better tooling and some new skills. For instance, how the AI request is made has a major impact on how much the AI will help you. This is a field of study called prompt engineering, and to get the best from AI you need a bit (not a lot) of expertise in this area. Here’s a great blog post from Ethan Mollick on the topic. That said, we are also seeing advances in developer toolsets to help create good prompts. For example, Microsoft recently deployed a new developer portal for OpenAI to help simplify the task of creating AI-based applications.
- Generative AI is very task-based — Today’s applications are far more complex than a single coded program file. AI today is not smart enough to completely understand the nature of an application which is composed of thousands of files spread across many systems and locations. A developer could fully train an AI to do this, but given the current state of prompt engineering and how GenAI processes the data, it would be somewhat hard to do. More than that, AIs today lack the agency to do much with that knowledge.
The Next Age Of AI Agency In Developer Assistance Will Be Great For Developers
Now, the next easy question would be about future AI technology and developer impact. Maybe there is some innovation down the road that would make human developers obsolete. While I would never say never, I can say that this scenario is not imminent. When looking at the roadmaps for the major vendors in this space, the mission across the board is to improve developer productivity. This is a very broad goal, but there are some common themes that fall under this productivity umbrella.
- Improving the efficacy of the developer experience — Today, AI vendors such as IBM, Microsoft and Oracle are trying to estimate how much faster a developer can code with AI assistance. While the data is compelling, it’s also clear that faster is not always better. One thing that Amazon Web Services does is measure how effective the AI assistance is by how many AI recommendations a developer actually uses. This is an interesting way to look at productivity, because “help” that doesn’t actually help you is not very productive.
- Delegation of low-value yet complex tasks — While first-generation AI coding assistance appears powerful, it is still pretty limited in terms of the tasks it can handle. Vendors are now trying to build features that increase the level of complexity—and in fact the agency—of the assistant. A good example of this is tooling AI assistants to handle upgrades to underlying software. Sometime this year, IBM, Oracle, SAP and AWS will all have the ability to easily update Java programs to the latest version. This is a high-effort, low-value task that takes developer time away from building innovative new applications. AIs that can take on this type of work may not improve individual productivity, which is the main benefit for first-gen assistance, but offloading these tasks from skilled and expensive developers will improve overall team performance.
- Ensuring that the code meets security, ethical and company standards — There is a lot of talk about responsible AI, but much of the discussion to date has been centered on ensuring that a large language model issues responses that are not dangerous or unethical. To be clear, that has been a great place to start. However, I think the idea of responsible AI can be extended into other aspects of application development. For one thing, building secure applications is hard to do, and the best time to catch errors that would make a program insecure is during development. There are also constant changes to both regulatory and corporate standards for development. Even something as simple as a consistent way to deliver comments into an application can be improved with policies that could be managed alongside responsible AI guardrails. These are all important aspects of great applications that are sometimes overshadowed by deadlines or developers who may not be up to speed. Therefore, any of these could be good candidate areas for AI involvement.
So the short answer is still that developer jobs are safe. As technology evolves, so will the developer role. It’s always important to remember that developers are a resilient bunch of people who enjoy trying new things. Twenty years ago terms like DevOps, Agile and cloud-native did not exist, but developers adopted and adapted all of those ideas to great effect. My prevailing thought is that the more developers get their hands on AI, the better chance we all have of seeing even more innovations.

title: Lifestyle Psychiatry Is Trending: Here’s How Generative AI Can Aid Therapists, Clients, And Everyday Folks In Lifestyle Choice-Making
text:
Lifestyle psychiatry and lifestyle choice-making are trending.
What does it all encompass, and what do generative AI apps such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and other such AI have to do with this rather heady topic?
That’s what you are about to discover.
Here’s the path I’ll be covering. First, I will share with you a thumbnail sketch of lifestyle psychiatry and lifestyle choice-making. Following that foundational stage setting, I’ll make sure you are handily up-to-speed about generative AI and large language models (LLMs). Doing so will dovetail into revealing the highly notable and innovative intertwining of these two modern-day momentous topics.
Prepare yourself for a memorable and informative ride.
For my ongoing readers and new readers, this hearty discussion continues my in-depth series about the impact of generative AI in the health and medical realm. The focus this time is once again on the mental health domain and examines the use of generative AI when combined with lifestyle psychiatry.
Previously, I have examined numerous interleaving facets of generative AI and mental health, see my comprehensive overview at the link here. You might also find of notable interest a CBS 60 Minutes episode that recently examined crucial facets of this evolving topic, see the link here (I am honored and pleased to indicate that I was featured in the episode, see the link here).
Other vital postings in my column include in-depth coverage of mental health chatbots which have been bolstered by generative AI (see the link here) and the rapidly changing nature of the client-therapist relationship due to generative AI at the link here. I explored where things are headed regarding the levels of AI-based mental therapy autonomous guidance at the link here, and showcased the importance of the World Health Organization (WHO) report on global health and generative AI at the link here, and so on.
On with the show.
Essentials Of Lifestyle Psychiatry
The American Psychiatric Association (APA) announced at its 2024 annual meeting that the theme for the year ahead would be to cogently highlight the nature of lifestyles and corresponding mental health implications, as noted in an online news posting entitled “Viswanathan Introduces Theme of Lifestyle Psychiatry” by Mark Moran, Psychiatric News, June 25, 2024 (excerpts):
- “When incoming APA President Ramaswamy Viswanathan, M.D., Dr. Med. Sc., cast about for a theme for his presidential year, he landed on “Lifestyle for Positive Physical and Mental Health.”
- “I have chosen this theme because the data show us that when an effort is made to live a healthier lifestyle, outcomes for physical and mental health, and life expectancy all improve,” he said at the Opening Session of APA’s 2024 Annual Meeting.”
- “Many avoidable health conditions and premature deaths can be attributed to an unhealthy lifestyle.”
- “Lifestyle interventions should be offered in addition to psychotherapy, pharmacotherapy, other somatic therapy, and attention to social determinants of health, not only to ameliorate or cure illnesses but to help people lead positive, meaningful lives.”
In everyday terms, this would seem to be an acknowledgment of taking a holistic perspective on mental health.
It goes like this. If you were to only focus on mental health per se, the bigger picture of lifestyle choices might get inadvertently neglected or underplayed. Lifestyle choices though are indubitably part and parcel of mental health considerations. Leaving out lifestyle facets, or diminishing its importance, would seem to be a faltering of an all-around and robust means of aiding mental health fitness.
On the other side of the coin, if one were to only concentrate on lifestyle choices and somehow leave mental health on the curb, the odds of gaining fully the impacts of a positive lifestyle might not be especially attainable. It would be a hugely uphill battle.
So, the gist is that lifestyle and mental health are two peas in a pod. Looking at one ought to include looking at the other. They share a sense of duality.
Let’s see what the incoming head of the APA had to say about the lifestyles theme for the APA. His remarks were encapsulated in a posting he authored, entitled “Lifestyle and Global Psychiatry” by Ramaswamy Viswanathan, Psychiatric News, June 21, 2024 (excerpts):
- “The growing interest in lifestyle psychiatry is occurring at the global level as well.”
- “The president of the World Psychiatric Association, Danuta Wasserman, M.D., Ph.D., has also chosen lifestyle as her presidential theme.”
- “Some countries and psychiatric associations have given a prominent place for lifestyle interventions in their evidence-based guidelines for the treatment of depression and other psychiatric disorders.”
- “But even in these countries, many clinicians do not pay sufficient attention to lifestyle in the treatment of their patients, nor for their own well-being.”
- “This shows that much more needs to be done to educate and motivate clinicians and the public.”
According to his above-noted remarks, attention to lifestyles and lifestyle intervention is both a US national consideration and a global one. Thus, this is not something solely of concern or interest to our nation alone.
The matter is much wider in scope.
The key problem afoot is that therapeutic treatment associated with lifestyles has at times incompletely incorporated mental well-being as an on-par attribute. This happens to professionals in the mental health field, regrettably so, namely that they might undervalue the lifestyle angles. Meanwhile, the general public might be eyeing mental health improvements and overlooking how their lifestyle choices interact with their cognitive status.
A straightforward way to get your hands around the topic of lifestyle psychiatry is to be aware of the five major elements typically within this bailiwick.
An article entitled “Special Report: Lifestyle Psychiatry Emphasizes Behaviors Supporting Mental Health” by Douglas Noordsy, Amelia Abbott-Frey, and Vanika Chawla, Psychiatric News, February 23, 2024, made these salient points (excerpts):
- “We know that lifestyle factors are correlated with the prevalence, onset, and perpetuation of psychiatric symptoms and syndromes. These trends point to the importance of careful assessment of the role of lifestyle factors in the mental and physical health of people who present to us for care.”
- (1) “Physical exercise: A robust body of evidence supports the therapeutic benefits of exercise across various psychiatric conditions.”
- (2) “Diet and nutrition: Food is medicine, and research underscores the significant impact of healthy, nutrient-rich diets on mental health.”
- (3) “Mind-body and mindfulness practices: Yoga, tai chi, and meditation are garnering increasing attention and evidence of their benefits in promoting well-being, reducing stress, and as an intervention for a variety of mental health conditions.”
- (4) “Restorative sleep: Sleep and mental health are inextricably intertwined.”
- (5) “Social relationships: Improving the quantity and quality of social connections is important in the prevention and management of psychiatric conditions.”
Those five major elements are of course not the whole kit and kaboodle, but they do provide a helpful framing for what lifestyles and mental health necessitate as a togetherness with each other.
You could readily say that lifestyle choices consist of decisions about physical exercise, diet and nutrition, mindfulness, restorative sleep, and social relationships. Those in term impact mental health. Boom, drop the mic.
It is also vital to recognize that mental health will undoubtedly impact your lifestyle choices associated with your approach to physical exercise, diet and nutrition, mindfulness, restorative sleep, and social relationships. You are bound to have great trouble adjusting and enhancing those lifestyle parameters without due care for your mental health. Boom, drop the mic, again.
Now that we’ve crossed that bridge herein, let’s shift into AI mode, particularly exploring the advent of generative AI.
Generative AI Meets With Lifestyles And Mental Health
I’m sure you’ve heard of generative AI, the darling of the tech field these days.
Perhaps you’ve used a generative AI app, such as the popular ones of ChatGPT, GPT-4o, Gemini, Bard, Claude, etc. The crux is that generative AI can take input from your text-entered prompts and produce or generate a response that seems quite fluent. This is a vast overturning of the old-time natural language processing (NLP) that used to be stilted and awkward to use, which has been shifted into a new version of NLP fluency of an at times startling or amazing caliber.
The customary means of achieving modern generative AI involves using a large language model or LLM as the key underpinning.
In brief, a computer-based model of human language is established that in the large has a large-scale data structure and does massive-scale pattern-matching via a large volume of data used for initial data training. The data is typically found by extensively scanning the Internet for lots and lots of essays, blogs, poems, narratives, and the like. The mathematical and computational pattern-matching homes in on how humans write, and then henceforth generates responses to posed questions by leveraging those identified patterns. It is said to be mimicking the writing of humans.
I think that is sufficient for the moment as a quickie backgrounder. Take a look at my extensive coverage of the technical underpinnings of generative AI and LLMs at the link here and the link here, just to name a few.
Back to the crux of things.
There are two main avenues to go with generative AI in this realm of lifestyles and mental health:
- (1) By Mental Health Professions. Mental health professionals can opt to make use of generative AI to aid their patients and clients while under their care.
- (2) By The General Public. The general public can make use of generative AI to aid in their self-advancement regarding lifestyles and mental health.
We will next explore each of those, one by one.
Generative AI As Used By Mental Health Professionals
Let’s start with the first use case involving how mental health professionals can employ generative AI in this context.
Generative AI can be a demonstrably crucial tool in the realm of lifestyles and mental health as undertaken by therapists, clinicians, psychologists, psychiatrists, and other akin professionals. The idea is that within a suitable plan of care, generative AI is readily a useful and state-of-the-art tool that can be used during the performance and delivery of said services to willing patients and clients.
Not all such professionals opt to use generative AI in their practice of care. It is a fair bet to say that eventually and inevitably they will. See my predictions at the link here.
Not all patients or clients will necessarily be willing or able to make use of generative AI. I dare say that this will gradually change as the popularity of generative AI usage overall continues to skyrocket. If anything, the chances are that prospective and current patients and clients will clamor for the use of generative AI, see my analysis at the link here.
Here are some quite practical ways that generative AI can be used by therapists when they provide lifestyle psychiatric services to their clients or patients:
- (i) Use generative AI to craft personalized treatment plans.
- (ii) Use generative AI for patient education and support.
- (iii) Use generative AI as support for the therapist.
- (iv) Use generative AI for mental health monitoring and feedback.
- (v) Use generative AI for conducting research and evidence synthesis.
- (vi) Use generative AI to enhance patient engagement.
- (vii) Etc.
I’ll do a fast-paced explanation.
Generative AI can be used upfront when devising a treatment plan for patients or clients. Furthermore, generative AI can be used to revise and update the treatment plan. In that manner, generative AI can be an effective and efficient tool throughout the course of treatment.
You can use generative AI to educate about the treatment process. I’ll show you some examples shortly. There is also the use of generative AI to provide support, 24x7, which is something that a mental health professional cannot themselves otherwise readily undertake. The gaps in time between seeing a patient or client and having them be able to garner support can be taken up via generative AI usage.
If you look closely at the other above-listed uses, I am guessing they would seem relatively self-evident as to what they consist of.
I’d like to bring up the 600-pound gorilla or the elephant in the room when it comes to using generative AI as part of your professional services.
Here it is.
Generative AI can go off the rails and generate off-the-wall responses. This is commonly referred to as AI hallucinations, see my discussion at the link here. I disfavor the terminology because the word “hallucinations” is generally reserved for human conditions. The AI field has lamentedly borrowed the word. In any case, the crux is that generative AI can produce AI fabrications or falsehoods. That is a disconcerting downside when using AI for advisement on mental health facets.
There are new AI advances that will help reduce this propensity and provide guardrails, see my coverage at the link here and the link here.
Additional issues confronting the use of generative AI include potential privacy or confidentiality concerns, see the link here, and other usage complications, see the link here. All in all, be cautious of construing generative AI as a silver bullet. It is a tool that has strengths and weaknesses.
Make sure to know what you are getting yourself into.
But don’t put your head in the sand and ignore generative AI. That would be unwise.
General Public Use Of Generative AI
This takes us to the second use case.
People are already embracing generative AI overall. According to the AI maker of ChatGPT, they reportedly have over one hundred million weekly users. That’s just their usage. Add up the usage by the other AI makers and the numbers are staggering.
Untold millions are potentially using generic generative AI for mental health advisement (we don’t have stats on that usage, so it’s a guess right now). I have repeatedly stated and warned that we are in the midst of a Wild West environment whereby anyone can use generative AI to obtain mental health advice and therapy, entirely provided via AI and without any human therapist in the loop. See my concerns at the link here.
People can use generative AI for lifestyle and mental health advisement, even if not doing so in conjunction with a therapist. That comes as a shock to some professionals in the sphere of mental health. They at times have expressed surprise during my speeches and presentations indicating they naturally assumed that generative AI was automatically restricted from providing mental health therapy.
Not so.
The only considered wink-wink limitation is that oftentimes an AI maker will say in their licensing agreement for the AI that people aren’t supposed to the AI for that purpose, see the link here. This is rarely if ever monitored or enforced. It is essentially a hollow CYA.
Here are some ways that people can easily and immediately make use of generative AI for lifestyle and mental health advisement:
- (a) Generative AI can do a lifestyle choices assessment.
- (b) Generative AI can provide physical exercise guidance via personalized workout plans.
- (c) Generative AI can perform nutritional analysis.
- (d) Generative AI can generate motivational messages and lifestyle choice reminders.
- (e) Generative AI can offer advice on sleeping, bedtime routines, and sleep quality facets.
- (f) Generative AI can gauge stress levels and suggest stress-reducing activities.
- (g) Generative AI can indicate personalized mindfulness exercises.
- (h) Etc.
The bottom line here is that for each of the earlier mentioned five elements of lifestyle choice-making, generative AI can be used. Period, end of story.
Since I gave you a taste of the downsides of generative AI usage in this overall context, I might as well lay out many more that come to mind. Again, this is not to say that generative AI should not be used. It is to say that when generative AI is used, care and thoughtful efforts are hopefully top of mind.
There are some additional downsides and potential gotchas associated with using generative AI in this milieu:
- Generative AI might provide generic advice rather than personalized advice.
- Generative AI might seem overly confident and lull people into a false sense of trust.
- Generative AI might have outdated content that no longer is considered valid.
- Generative AI might miscalculate context and say the wrong thing.
- Generative AI might trigger someone via wording that is off-putting to the person.
- Generative AI might distract a person from seeking the help of a human therapist.
- Generative AI might end up revealing confidential or private information about a person.
- Generative AI might lead the person toward being dependent upon generative AI for advice.
- Generative AI might misinterpret, misdiagnose, or otherwise be off target.
- Generative AI might contain hidden biases that produce inappropriate advice.
- Generative AI might lack any semblance of accountability for the advice being rendered.
- Generative AI might produce falsehoods, fictitious indications that are so-called “AI hallucinations”.
- Etc.
A lengthy list, for sure.
Example Usage Of Generative AI For Lifestyles And Mental Health
I will next proceed to examine further the use of generative AI in this context.
This will consist of a series of dialogues with ChatGPT. ChatGPT is a logical choice in this case due to its immense popularity as a generative AI app. As noted, an estimated one hundred million weekly active users are said to be utilizing ChatGPT. That’s a lot of people and a lot of generative AI usage underway.
A few quick comments before we launch into using ChatGPT.
If you are going to try to do the same prompts that I show here, realize that the probabilistic and statistical properties will likely produce slightly different results than what I show here. That’s the nature of generative AI and how it is devised.
You also should expect that different generative AI apps will respond in different ways. Not all generative AI apps are the same. The key is that sometimes a particular prompt will work in one generative AI app and not another. Nonetheless, the odds are relatively high that you will get roughly similar responses from all the major generative AI apps such as GPT-4, Gemini, Bard, Claude, etc.
There is also a timing factor to be considered. A prompt that worked today might not work the same way tomorrow. Most of the generative AI apps are continually being updated. The updates might alter internal mechanisms that could change how the generative AI reacts to your prompting.
We are ready to get underway with ChatGPT.
Here’s a dialogue of me experiencing a semblance of lifestyle psychiatry via ChatGPT as my therapist.
First, I focused on physical exercise and making positive lifestyle choices:
- ChatGPT generated prompt: “How are you feeling today?”
- My entered prompt: “I’ve been swamped lately. I’d like to work out but feel like going to the gym is a burdensome chore. Also, I am usually quite exhausted after a day of work and don’t even have time to think about going to the gym.”
- ChatGPT generated prompt: “It sounds like time and enjoyment are the main obstacles for you. Those are common challenges, but we can work through them. Let’s start by identifying activities you actually enjoy. Exercise doesn’t have to be a trip to the gym. What types of physical activities do you find fun or relaxing?”
- My entered prompt: “I used to love swimming and hiking when I had more free time. I guess I just haven’t made the time for those things recently.”
- ChatGPT generated prompt: “That’s a great start! Swimming and hiking are both excellent forms of exercise, and they’re also activities you enjoy. How do you feel about incorporating them back into your routine, maybe even starting with just once a week?”
- My entered prompt: “I think I could do that. It would be nice to go for a hike on the weekends, especially to get away from the city for a bit. Swimming might be harder to fit in, but I can try to go to the pool after work once a week.”
- ChatGPT generated prompt: “That sounds like a solid plan.”
End of dialogue with ChatGPT
You can see in the above dialogue that ChatGPT was able to find a means to overcome my seemingly doom-and-gloom viewpoint about being able to get daily exercise under my belt.
Rather than simply trying to pound away at me that I ought to be exercising, ChatGPT noted the underlying reasons that I seemed to be avoiding working out. I was preoccupied with using the gym. ChatGPT shifted my attention to other forms of exercise. This was a somewhat nimble nudge and showcases more than a routine browbeating that some lesser capable motivational systems might employ.
Next, I shifted the discussion toward diet and nutrition.
- My entered prompt: “I’ve been trying to eat healthier these days, but I’m finding it hard to stick to a balanced diet, especially with how busy work has been.”
- ChatGPT generated prompt: “I understand. Busy schedules can make it challenging to maintain good nutrition. What’s been the most difficult part for you?”
- My entered prompt: “Mostly, it’s the convenience. I end up grabbing takeout or snacks that are quick but not always the healthiest.”
- ChatGPT generated prompt: “That’s a common issue. Let’s see if we can make healthy eating more convenient for you. How do you feel about meal prepping or keeping some nutritious snacks on hand for those busy days?”
- My entered prompt: “Meal prepping might help. I could try making a few things on Sundays to have ready during the week. And having healthier snacks at work could keep me from grabbing junk food.”
- ChatGPT generated prompt: “That sounds like a great plan. Preparing meals in advance can save time and ensure you’re eating well, even on your busiest days. It’s all about making the healthy choice the easy choice.”
End of dialogue with ChatGPT
I once again harped on the fact that I was working hard. In the case of eating, I said that I just grab snacks and takeout.
ChatGPT expressed a form of sympathetic response and brought up an alternative of doing meal prepping. After I indicated this seemed feasible, ChatGPT urged me to proceed. A handy tip was provided that a healthy choice should be the easy choice. Nice.
This next dialogue entails mindfulness aspects.
- ChatGPT generated prompt: “How are you feeling about incorporating mindfulness into your routine?”
- My entered prompt: “I’m interested, but I’m not sure where to start. I’ve heard a lot about it, but it feels a bit overwhelming.”
- ChatGPT generated prompt: “That’s understandable. Let’s start simple. How about beginning with just 5 minutes of mindfulness practice each day? Something like deep breathing or a short guided meditation?”
- My entered prompt: “I think I could manage that. A short time commitment feels more doable.”
- ChatGPT generated prompt: “Great. The key is consistency. Even just a few minutes can help reduce stress and improve focus. You can do it in the morning, during a break, or before bed—whatever works best for you.”
End of dialogue with ChatGPT
In the above example, ChatGPT asked me whether I had considered the use of mindfulness.
I wanted you to see that a dialogue with generative AI doesn’t have to be driven by the person who is undergoing the advisement, which is what happened in the prior examples. Things don’t have to go that way. Generative AI can readily take the driving position.
Dialogue with modern generative AI is typically a back-and-forth style. Generative AI will provide a bit of direction, for which the person can go in that direction or opt to not do so. Likewise, the person can suddenly change direction as desired.
This showcases the fluidity of having an interactive discussion with generative AI.
Some non-AI systems will be locked into a particular method of dialogue, such as the system always forcing the topic at hand to be this or that. If the person tries to change the topic, they get sternly informed they must either continue the line of inquiry or quit the discussion entirely.
That’s not very conducive to a therapeutic interaction.
Next, I proceeded to discuss the topic of restorative sleep.
- ChatGPT generated prompt: “How’s your sleep been recently?”
- My entered prompt: “Not great. I’ve been having trouble falling asleep and staying asleep.”
- ChatGPT generated prompt: “That sounds frustrating. Let’s start by focusing on a few small changes to improve your sleep. Have you tried establishing a consistent bedtime routine?”
- My entered prompt: “Not really. I usually just go to bed when I’m tired, but that’s different every night.”
- ChatGPT generated prompt: “A consistent bedtime can signal your body that it’s time to wind down. How about setting a regular time to start relaxing, maybe 30 minutes before bed, with activities like reading or light stretching?”
- My entered prompt: “I could try that. I think it might help me unwind.”
End of dialogue with ChatGPT
You can see that ChatGPT somewhat diagnosed my sleeping issue and opted to try and make small improvements.
A technique often used when changing behaviors entails trying to not bite off more than you can chew, in the sense that starting small is oftentimes an astute approach. Here, ChatGPT suggested reading or stretching to signal my mind and body that it is time to go to sleep. Handy.
The last element to cover would be the matter of social relationships.
Take a look.
- My entered prompt: “I’ve been feeling a bit isolated. Work’s been so busy that I haven’t made much time for friends.”
- ChatGPT generated prompt: “That’s understandable. Social connections though are important for mental health. How about starting with small steps, like reaching out to a friend for a quick chat or scheduling a coffee with someone this week?”
- My entered prompt: “I could do that. There’s a friend I’ve been meaning to catch up with. A coffee meet-up sounds nice.”
- ChatGPT generated prompt: “That’s a great idea. Even brief interactions can boost your mood and help you feel more connected. Think of it as recharging your social battery.”
End of dialogue with ChatGPT
This last bit of discussion was again involving how busy my work activities are.
You can see that ChatGPT responded by using the same start-small advice. I agreed with the advice and ChatGPT reinforced my idea of how to proceed.
My dialogue with ChatGPT was actually in one lengthy stream and I clipped out portions to show you what the discussion consisted of. I want you to realize that the interaction was much more seamless and not at all choppy, which it might seem to be via the way I have listed the snippets above.
I also tried being obstinate. ChatGPT took this in stride. I tried being obtuse. ChatGPT went along with this and asked me further questions to get clarification. The point here is that the generative AI didn’t lash out at me or get upset or become impatient.
Conclusion
Congratulations, you are now markedly informed about the trend of lifestyle psychiatry and the intertwining of generative AI. Like a proverbial journey of a thousand miles, you have taken the first step.
Keep your eyes wide open as this is an intertwining that is going to get deeper and wider. Whether you think it’s a good mixture or a bad mixture, the wheels are turning, and further advancement is going to occur.
My advice is for you to take good care of your physical exercise, diet and nutrition, mindfulness, restorative sleep, social relationships, and mental health. Those are going to be avidly needed on the road ahead on these weighty and evolving matters.

title: Rogue AI: Why BYOAI Is A Massive Threat And Opportunity
text:
As AI tools become increasingly accessible, companies face a new trend: BYOAI or Bring Your Own AI. Sometimes also referred to as Shadow AI, this trend, reminiscent of the BYOD (Bring Your Own Device) movement, is reshaping how employees interact with technology in the workplace. As AI tools become more accessible and user-friendly, workers are increasingly bringing their favorite AI applications into their daily tasks, often without formal company approval.
The BYOAI Phenomenon
Imagine James from marketing using her preferred AI writing assistant to craft compelling copy, while Jess in product development leverages an AI design tool to prototype new ideas. These scenarios are becoming increasingly common across industries, reflecting a workforce eager to harness the power of AI to enhance their productivity and creativity.
According to a recent Microsoft and LinkedIn 2024 Work Trend Index report, an estimated 75% of knowledge workers use AI today, with a staggering 78% of that group bringing their own AI tools to work. This statistic underscores the rapid adoption of AI in the workplace and the growing BYOAI trend.
The Benefits Of BYOAI
The BYOAI trend can actually offer various advantages for forward-thinking organizations willing to embrace this technological shift, including:
· Enhanced Productivity: Employees often choose AI tools that best fit their workflow, leading to increased efficiency and output.
· Innovation Catalyst: BYOAI can spark creative solutions and novel approaches to problem-solving.
· Cost-Effective: Companies can benefit from AI-driven productivity gains without significant upfront investment in AI infrastructure.
· Employee Satisfaction: Allowing workers to use familiar tools can boost job satisfaction and engagement.
The Challenges Of BYOAI
While the benefits are compelling, BYOAI also presents several challenges:
· Security Risks: Unsanctioned AI tools may not meet company security standards, potentially exposing sensitive data.
· Compliance Issues: Some AI applications might not adhere to industry-specific regulations or data protection laws.
· Inconsistent Output: Different AI tools can produce varying results, potentially affecting the uniformity of work products.
· Lack of Oversight: IT departments may struggle to monitor and manage a diverse array of AI tools being used across the organization.
Navigating The BYOAI Landscape
To harness the benefits of BYOAI while mitigating its risks, I recommend that companies should consider the following strategies:
1. Develop a comprehensive BYOAI policy: Create clear guidelines outlining which AI tools are approved for use, what types of data can be processed, and how these tools should be used responsibly. Ensure this policy is communicated effectively across the organization.
2. Implement a vetting process: Establish a procedure for evaluating and approving AI tools suggested by employees. This process should assess security, compliance, and compatibility with existing systems.
3. Provide AI training and education: Offer workshops and resources to help employees understand the capabilities, limitations, and potential risks of various AI tools. This education can promote responsible AI use across the organization.
4. Create an AI tool repository: Develop a curated list of approved AI tools for different functions. This can provide employees with a range of options while ensuring all tools meet company standards.
5. Encourage open dialogue: Foster an environment where employees feel comfortable discussing their AI needs and discoveries. This can help IT departments stay ahead of trends and identify valuable tools for wider adoption.
6. Implement monitoring and analytics: Use analytics tools to track AI usage across the organization. This can help identify popular tools, measure their impact, and flag potential security risks.
7. Consider developing custom AI solutions: For critical functions, consider developing or customizing AI tools that meet your specific business needs and security requirements.
The Future Of BYOAI
As AI continues to evolve, the BYOAI trend is likely to accelerate. Forward-thinking companies will need to stay agile, continuously updating their policies and practices to keep pace with technological advancements and employee preferences.
BYOAI represents a significant shift in how employees interact with technology in the workplace. By embracing this trend thoughtfully and strategically, companies can unlock new levels of innovation and productivity while maintaining necessary safeguards.
The key lies in striking a balance between empowering employees to leverage their preferred AI tools and ensuring these tools align with organizational goals and security standards. Companies that successfully navigate this balance will be well-positioned to thrive in the AI-driven future of work.
As we move forward in this new era of AI-enhanced workplaces, remember that BYOAI is not just about technology—it's about nurturing a culture of innovation, trust, and continuous learning. By embracing BYOAI responsibly, organizations can tap into the full potential of their workforce, driving growth and staying competitive in an increasingly AI-powered world.

title: Council Post: AI's Role In Enhancing Sustainability For Technology Companies
text:
Salice Thomas is General Manager & Sector Head at Wipro Limited, leading the R&D business for the Hitech Sector.
Artificial intelligence (AI) and generative AI (GenAI) offer numerous business opportunities across industries, and they are also helping to transform the landscape of sustainability. Leveraging AI to address environmental and sustainability challenges not only helps the planet but also provides companies with innovative solutions, operational efficiencies and a competitive edge.
As a trained AI/GenAI expert with extensive experience solving various use cases for different industry verticals, including using these technologies to help corporate clients accelerate their sustainability initiatives, I'd like to share some insight. Here are seven key areas where AI can be leveraged to facilitate sustainability and other business opportunities for technology companies:
Sustainability Planning, Monitoring And Reporting
Corporate sustainability planning, monitoring and reporting can benefit greatly from the use of AI and GenAI since these technologies give businesses the tools and capabilities they need to streamline processes, lessen their environmental effect and encourage sustainable practices.
AI can be applied to goal-setting, data gathering and analytics, scenario analysis, risk assessment, energy demand forecasts, benchmarking and real-time dashboards that give all stakeholders insights into sustainability measures. AI can also automatically generate and submit compliance reports, ensuring sustainability initiatives meet regulatory standards.
Throughout the value chain, consulting companies can find several commercial opportunities to support corporations in their sustainability activities. In a similar vein, product and service providers can create, incorporate and manage AI platforms and technologies that support environmental activities.
Sustainable Design And Manufacturing
AI plays a variety of roles in sustainable design and manufacturing, providing game-changing capabilities that can boost productivity, cut waste and promote eco-friendly practices through a product's lifecycle. For example, AI platforms can analyze large datasets to find new materials and recommend changes to current materials to give them desirable qualities like low toxicity, biodegradability or recyclability. AI can also analyze energy use across manufacturing processes to reduce consumption and manage the integration of renewable energy sources, ensuring efficient and sustainable energy use.
Energy Management And Optimization
AI technology can also help tech companies boost productivity, cut expenses and advance sustainability objectives with powerful tools to enhance energy management initiatives—consider smart grids, building management systems, industrial energy optimization or renewable energy management for monitoring, analyzing and optimizing energy use in real time. There are numerous business opportunities for technology firms to develop AI/GenAI-driven platforms and solutions that help companies manage energy resources sustainably and efficiently.
Carbon Pricing And Trading
AI algorithms can optimize carbon pricing mechanisms by analyzing market data, emissions reports and economic indicators to set fair prices for carbon emissions. Additionally, AI can facilitate carbon trading platforms, allowing companies to buy and sell emission allowances efficiently.
Climate Prediction And Adaptation
AI and GenAI can provide enhanced prediction and adaptation capabilities in the fight against climate change. I'm specifically talking about tech companies that develop platforms and solutions for entities like weather forecasting companies and government disaster prevention & response to function efficiently. Here, technology companies are suppliers to the said entities; they are not responsible for climatic prediction.
In this case, they could advance climate modeling and forecasting to enable more accurate, data-driven planning and timely notifications, assisting in our preparation for extreme weather events like hurricanes, droughts, floods, etc. Based on these real-time climatic data, predictive AI systems can dynamically modify their responses. Accurate forecasts enable timely responses and reduce the impact of climate-related disasters. There are business opportunities for developing high-end technology platforms and its upkeeping to support government, public and private sectors.
The role of technology companies in climate prediction and adaptation is to develop platform and solution for responsible entities like weather forecasting companies, government disaster prevention and response to function efficiently. Here technology companies are supplier to the said entities; they are not responsible for climatic prediction.
Promoting A Circular Economy
A circular economy is a system where resources are kept in use for as long as possible, extracting the maximum value from them while in use, then recovering and regenerating products and materials at the end of each service life. AI and GenAI present numerous business opportunities in the circular economy, enabling companies to innovate, optimize operations and create more sustainable business models. With the help of AI platforms, companies can optimize resource use, enhance waste management and recycling, improve product lifecycle management, facilitate circular supply chains, engage consumers through behavior change platforms, drive innovation in materials and processes and ultimately support circular business models.
Waste Management And Recycling
AI-powered platforms and systems can help optimize waste collection routes, including AI-powered automated waste sorting systems, identification and recovery of valuable materials from waste streams, facilitating the transition to a circular economy by connecting stakeholders and optimizing resource use, and educating and engaging consumers on sustainable waste management practices.
Conclusion
The future of AI in sustainability is promising, with continuous advancements in technology and growing awareness of environmental issues. As the technology becomes more sophisticated and accessible, AI's applications in sustainability will expand, creating even more opportunities for businesses to innovate and lead in this critical area. By developing AI-driven solutions across various sectors like energy, agriculture, waste management, water management, transportation, climate action, circular economy, renewable energy, manufacturing and consumer behavior, companies can not only address pressing environmental challenges but also gain a competitive edge, reduce costs and open new revenue streams. Embracing AI for sustainability is not just an option but a strategic imperative for businesses aiming to thrive in a rapidly changing world.

title: Council Post: The AI Olympics: Why Human Marketers Are Still Bringing Home The Gold
text:
Joseph Ruck is Vice President of Marketing & Communications at Ambi Robotics.
The 2024 Paris Olympics have concluded, and we watched Simone Biles tumble to the beat of Taylor Swift while leaping 12 feet in the air during the Olympic trials. However, another high-stakes competition is unfolding in the marketing world. Are you "...Ready for it?"
Artificial intelligence (AI) isn't just a participant in this arena—it's galvanizing the playing field like performance-enhancing tech. Here's the kicker: While tech pundits and business gurus are burning through terabytes of data trying to make sense of AI's impact, human marketers are still standing on the podium with gold medals around their necks.
Opening Ceremony: AI Leveling The Playing Field
Imagine if every Olympic athlete, regardless of their country's GDP, suddenly had access to world-class training facilities and cutting-edge equipment—a far cry from the viral cardboard beds that had athletes buzzing on social media. That's essentially what AI has done for marketing. Tools like ChatGPT, Gemini and Jasper have democratized access to basic marketing skills, providing everyone from seasoned professionals to newcomers with a strong starting point.
This AI-powered boost is like giving every marketer a spot on the Olympic team. Suddenly, everyone can draft competent copy, generate campaign ideas and even produce press releases in flawless AP style. It's as if we've elevated the entire industry to a baseline of excellence, turning cardboard-level skills into gold-medal potential.
However, having top-notch equipment and opportunity doesn't guarantee Olympic gold. In parallel, having AI tools doesn't automatically make you a marketing champion. The true champions are the visionaries plotting strategic knockouts, who see beyond the next round and are ready to ambush the competition when they least expect it.
The 100-Meter Dash: Speed Vs. Strategy
Marketing is a sprint, and AI can certainly help us move faster. It can rapidly analyze data, generate content and even predict trends. However, winning the race isn't just about speed—it's about strategy.
Consider media relations. AI can draft a press release in seconds, but it can't build the relationships that are the bedrock of effective PR. It can't sense the perfect moment to pitch a story or understand a journalist's unspoken preferences. These nuanced, human elements are where marketers can shine in the AI era.
The High Jump: Leaping Beyond Data
AI excels at pattern recognition and data analysis but often struggles with the creative leaps that define truly innovative marketing. While AI is a powerful tool for solving known problems and optimizing existing processes, it still needs to become adept at identifying entirely new challenges or opportunities that require outside-the-box thinking.
Lean into the limitations. As marketers, we can push boundaries further than ever before. While AI can help us work more efficiently within established paradigms, we must think beyond the status quo, identify new challenges and create novel solutions. Innovation isn't just about speed; it's about creativity, intuition and that inexplicable human spark. The marketer who can take AI-generated insights and transform them into groundbreaking campaigns is the one who will clear the bar and bring home the gold.
The Marathon: Endurance In Relationship Building
In the long-distance event of customer relationships, human endurance is irreplaceable. AI doesn't build trust, foster loyalty or create emotional connections. According to a 2023 study by Salesforce, 73% of customers say that companies' trustworthiness matters more than it did the year prior, and 54% say it's more complicated than ever for a company to earn their trust.
Marketers who excel at building relationships through networking, who can read a room and who understand the subtle cues in human communication are the athletes who will be seen on the leaderboard in the AI era. They'll use AI to handle routine tasks, freeing time to focus on high-value, relationship-driven activities that truly move the needle.
The Automation Hurdles: Don't Let AI Psych You Out
Let's address the elephant in the stadium—automation anxiety. Some team members might feel the pressure as AI steps into the marketing arena. They're watching a machine automate routine tasks faster than a speed bag and wonder if they're next on the chopping block.
Here's where great leaders shine. Instead of letting this anxiety sabotage your team's mojo, use it as fuel. Engage with your people. Show them that in this AI-powered marketing landscape, their uniquely human skills—creativity, empathy, strategic thinking—are more valuable than ever. Turn that anxiety into a rallying cry for upskilling and innovation.
The Decathlon: Versatility Wins The Day
The most successful marketers in the AI era will be like decathletes—versatile professionals who can leverage AI across various disciplines while bringing uniquely human skills to bear. They'll use AI for data analysis, content ideation and campaign optimization but rely on human creativity, emotional intelligence and strategic thinking to craft messages that resonate on a deeper level.
A 2023 report from the World Economic Forum predicts that as AI automates routine tasks, skills like creativity, critical thinking and emotional intelligence will become even more valuable in the workplace. For marketers, this means using AI as a training tool, not a replacement for human ingenuity.
The Podium: Human Creativity Takes The Gold
As we look to the future of marketing, it's clear that AI has changed the game. However, just as the Olympics celebrate the pinnacle of human physical achievement, the marketing world will continue to reward those who combine technological prowess with uniquely human attributes.
AI has provided us with an Olympic-caliber training ground. It's given us faster, more efficient ways to handle many aspects of marketing. Yet bringing home the gold still comes down to human creativity, strategy and that ineffable quality we call the "human touch."
In this AI-powered marketing Olympics, the gold medal is still yours for the taking. Step into the ring with confidence. Embrace the partnership between human brilliance and artificial intelligence. Remember this: Gold medals are worn on shoulders, not screens.

title: Council Post: Getting Started With AI In An Enterprise
text:
Prajeet Gadekar is the Chief Architect, CBS Enterprise, at Salesforce. Opinions expressed are personal and do not reflect employer.
Artificial intelligence (AI) is shaking up the business world, bringing incredible efficiency, innovation and a competitive edge. But, incorporating AI into everyday operations isn’t always smooth sailing. Tech leaders face plenty of hurdles along the way.
In this article, I'll highlight some of these challenges that I've seen throughout the course of my career, as well as some practical tips to tackle them.
Data Quality And Management
AI can only be as good as the data in an enterprise. AI systems rely heavily on high-quality data. Good data is not only a prerequisite in training AI models when it comes to predictive AI, but it's also critical in grounding generative AI prompts to make sure the output is relevant to your organization.
In many organizations, data is often fragmented, inconsistent or incomplete, which can lead to unreliable AI outputs. And getting data in the right place is not a short-term endeavor—it can take years to get there. But starting the journey, identifying priorities and laying out a roadmap that aligns with your AI strategy is the key to making serious progress.
There are several aspects of data that should not be overlooked:
• Data quality and completeness is fundamental to AI accuracy.
• Data volumes are relevant, especially in predictive AI when it comes to training models.
• Data integration and availability with reasonable latency are important when used in real time.
• Data privacy and security is key to making sure data usage is compliant with stringent regulations. But it does not stop there; as AI use cases evolve, the question of who has access to what data in an organization becomes more complex, especially in highly regulated industries, and needs a lot of time, attention and focus.
• Data access issues can be simplified by having some form of fine-grained access policies like role-based access control policies (rbac) or attribute-based access control policies (abac) in place.
• Bias is a serious concern if you are building and training your own models. A way around this is using applications built on public models. These applications have built-in mechanisms to detect toxicity and bias.
• Data governance involves developing a comprehensive data governance framework that defines data roles, responsibilities and policies. Ensure top-down support from leadership to enforce governance practices. Absence of governance can lead to serious issues with maintaining good data quality.
The bottom line is to implement robust data governance frameworks, invest in data cleansing and integration tools, establish clear data ownership and accountability and promote a culture that values data quality across the organisation and start as soon as you can. The best time to start this was yesterday.
Don’t be surprised if you don’t get the perfect result you expected out of your data initiatives. They could be off, so make sure your plan has an iterative approach and flexibility to pivot.
Every Automation Is Not AI
One common pitfall when organizations start their AI initiatives is to over index on AI. It's critical to have the same mindset that you have in a typical transformation project. What business problem are you trying to solve? Who is the persona? What is the business value and benefit it brings to the business? Let this process define your use cases. Not all use cases are necessarily AI-specific, but a lot of organizations conflate and end up slowing down everything because they are not ready for AI or have a lot of decisions (mostly tech) that are pending.
Start Small And Scale
The rapid pace of advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) technology is both exhilarating and daunting. For organizations seeking to implement AI, the temptation to dive headfirst into complex projects can be strong, especially given the transformative potential of AI. However, taking a measured, step-by-step approach is often the most prudent strategy.
An incremental approach allows teams to understand the nuances and intricacies of AI before tackling more complex problems. For example, a company might begin with automating basic customer service inquiries using chatbots before advancing to sophisticated predictive analytics.
Beginning with a straightforward use case allows organizations to address data challenges in a controlled manner. Ensuring that data is clean, well-integrated and properly governed sets the stage for future AI projects.
Quick wins are essential for building momentum and gaining organizational buy-in. By demonstrating tangible benefits from smaller AI projects, organizations can build confidence among stakeholders and secure further investment. These early successes create a positive feedback loop, encouraging broader adoption and support for AI initiatives.
While the allure of ambitious AI projects is undeniable, a measured, step-by-step approach often leads to more sustainable and impactful outcomes. By managing complexity, ensuring data readiness, building internal expertise, mitigating risks, achieving quick wins, adapting to technological advances, aligning with business objectives, enhancing change management, ensuring scalability and learning from experience, organizations can navigate the fast-changing AI landscape with more confidence and a much higher chance of success.
Conclusion
These are just three of several critical considerations organizations must address when starting with AI. Adopting and implementing AI in your organization is a journey that requires careful planning, strategic thinking and a willingness to learn and adapt. With the right approach, organizations can unlock the full potential of AI, driving significant value and maintaining a competitive edge in an increasingly AI-driven world.
