text:
Last meals are trending.
This is happening for reasons beyond the usually anticipated basis. You see, I would assume that most people instantly think about prisoners having a last meal. Sure, that still happens. But the attention on the topic is elsewhere in our modern world.
The deal is this.
Social media has taken the Last Meals conception by storm and opted to post endlessly and vociferously about what people ought to eat or ought to not eat for their final dining experience. Online streamers and influencers have developed Internet-based broadcasts that invite celebrities to appear on camera and talk about their envisioned last meal. In many cases, the show arranges for the meal to be put together and cooked while in the studio, such that the celebrity and the guest dine on the specified last meal during a quite enthralling feastful interview. Bon appetite!
Don’t worry, the celebrity featured on the show happily remains alive and well after the presumed last meal. This is all for fun. Plus, some do this for bragging rights.
I’d like to add another surprise to the feasting table.
Turns out that generative AI can be used to aid in identifying your very own personalized last meal. Rather than trying to come up with something enticing and edible by random thoughts alone, you can leverage generative AI to guide you along the arduous path of meal selection.
Easy-peasy.
In today’s column, I will highlight how generative AI enters this latest societal trend that is of keen fascination regarding last meals. Ongoing readers are likely aware that I periodically select a cultural trend and showcase the ways that generative AI veers into the timely topic. For example, you might find of interest my exploration of altered states of consciousness and generative AI, see the link here, and how to cope with the rise in stonewalling via applying generative AI, see the link here. For more overall see the link here.
On with the show.
Last Meals Come In All Shapes And Sizes
What comes to your mind regarding the situation or circumstances under which the topic of a said-to-be last meal tends to arise in conversation?
There are quite a number of circumstances and certainly more than you can shake a stick at.
I shall share with you my off-the-cuff list:
- (1) Last meal as intense symbolism.
- (2) Last meal as the final act of earthly existence.
- (3) Last meal as a choice made by condemned prisoners.
- (4) Last meal as an indicator of you and your values.
- (5) Last meal as a sign of culture and the times.
- (6) Last meal as an interesting puzzle to contemplate.
- (7) Last meal as social media content and engagement.
- (8) Last meal as a fun conceptual topic to discuss.
- (9) Last meal as a party game.
- Etc.
You can plainly see from the list that sometimes a last meal can be a symbolic act, allowing the person to make a bold statement of one kind or another. Whether others will grasp the meaning of the food items selected, well, it’s hard to say. Anyway, the person might believe in their mind that the choices are vitally significant.
There is a modern perspective of wanting to puzzle out the idea of a last meal. What should you have? What should you avoid? What would your friends say about your choices? What would strangers say? It is a fun concept to toss around. You can do this in your own mind or play a kind of game with family, friends, and acquaintances. Be aware that some find this topic disconcerting and macabre. Not everyone favors discussing last meals.
There is one universal truism about last meals.
Are you ready to know it?
People are always interested in knowing what last meal was chosen by this or that person.
Let’s take a brief look at some historically notable instances that took place for condemned prisoners at their request (these are variously cited throughout the Internet; their veracity is to be questioned):
- In 1793, Louis XVI of France had a last meal that supposedly consisted of chicken, beef, turnips, vegetables, glasses of wine, and sponge cake. He was soon thereafter at the receiving end of a guillotine. Was this food gone to waste or put toward a reasonable cause? You decide.
- A famous robber and murderer in Germany reportedly had just a half-dozen glasses of beer as a last meal in 1902. Maybe this reflects the fact that you don’t have to actually eat food for your last meal. Liquids alone might suffice.
- A female put to death in 1962 for crimes committed had opted to have a steak and salad. Perhaps some last meals can be quite short and brisk. No need to embellish a last meal, if you don’t want to.
- In 2019, a convicted felon in Florida opted for cheeseburgers, french fries, and bacon. In contemporary times, that seems exceedingly fitting.
Divining Your Own Last Meal
I wanted to bring those last meals to your attention so that you can start mulling over your own preferred last meal. I intended to say that in the most upbeat and optimistic way possible. Your last meal is undoubtedly far off in the future.
Time to unpack last meals.
First, it seems that there aren’t any confining rules per se. You can choose a boatload of food or just a tiny morsel. You can go with rich foods or pedestrian foods. The food items don’t necessarily have to be a main course and a dessert. Heck, it’s your last meal, go wild.
Second, do not use various prisoner's last meals as a guide. I say this because many prisons do have strict rules and conditions about last meals. Prison authorities often stipulate what can be chosen. Also, to sidestep the notion of this being a melancholy last meal, the vernacular is that the meal is simply a special meal.
Special, if you get the drift.
A tad more about prison last meals might catch your eye.
Any oddball requests are typically turned down. The last meal has to be something that the prison can reasonably make or obtain. This presumably stops those requests for a thousand fish sandwiches. In some cases, the prisoner has to pay partially for the cost of the meal or the whole kit and kaboodle. The lowest of the last meals is the situation wherein whatever is served in the prison cafeteria that day is the last meal for the one being executed. That’s the way the ball bounces sometimes.
Third, you presumably want to select foods that you like. The idea is that you are treating yourself since this is the last meal. I suppose you could choose foods you dislike, but I’m not sure that is the best way to go out. One exception might be to finally eat those super spicy items that you’ve avoided throughout your life. Hopefully, the spice won’t hit you before the end comes. For the first time in your life, you’ll suffer no stomach adversity for having taken a gut chance. Nice.
Fourth, there is a rough-and-tumble decision about whether the food is sending a message rather than merely being something to be eaten. After you are gone, will people judge you by the last meal? If so, do you care? If you do care, what do you want them to believe that the last meal says about your character, your life, your attitudes, and so on?
Not caring about what others think of your last meal would seem to be the freest way to make your food choices. Let others read into your selections as they might wish to do so. It’s of no active concern to you at that point.
Historical Significance Of Last Meals
You might be intrigued to know that there are research studies about last meals.
Sometimes, historically significant people or moments have occurred that entail a last meal.
In a research study about the last meal of Buddha, entitled “The Last Meal Of The Buddha” by R. Gordon Wasson and Wendy Doniger O'Flaherty, Journal of the American Oriental Society, October 1982, these salient points were made (excerpts):
- “That the Buddha was eating his last meal was known to everyone thereabouts: nothing that happened there could have escaped those within eye-reach nor have been forgotten by them, not least because of the awesome event to take place a few hours later, the Buddha's translation to Nirvana that he had been predicting for that night since he was in Vaisali three months before.”
- “The meal was served to him and his suite of monks by his host the metal-worker Cunda at Pava, a village that lay near Kusinara where the Mahaparinirvana — the "Great Decease" as the Rhys Davidses translated it — was scheduled to take place some hours later.”
The gist is that the actual items in the last meal of that historical setting involving Buddha remain open to debate. Scholars are still going back and forth about what was truly served. In the research study that I cited above, there are pages upon pages of nitty-gritty details carefully identified to try and systematically speculate what was eaten.
Moving on, an interesting legal study examined the rights and rituals associated with last meals. In a research paper entitled “Cold Comfort Food: A Systematic Examination of the Rituals and Rights of the Last Meal” by Sarah Gerwig-Moore, Mercer University School of Law, Mercer Law School Digital Commons, 2014, these points were made (excerpts):
- “When my co-authors and I first became interested in this project, we were first struck by the broad, pop-culture interest in the last meal. Some of the interest has been historical and academic, while some has been more sensational and voyeuristic.”
- “Although most believe the ritual originates with the last meal of Jesus Christ, according to Max Bigert, co-producer of the Swedish documentary Last Supper, the tradition “can be traced back to pre-Christian times, to the fear of ghosts. In Ancient Greece you had to feed the person who was going to be executed so that they could cross the River Styx into the underworld, and not come back as a hungry ghost.”
- “A meaningful final meal is not limited to people in prison. Many who know or suspect death is impending seek out meaningful rituals and traditions with loved ones — some of which include food.”
- “Even beyond the context of actual executions, considering a last meal has become a sort of get-to-know-you game.”
- “A few years ago, an article ran in Time Magazine relaying the questions asked by Melanie Dunea, in her book called “My Last Supper.” Dunea asked celebrities what they would order for their last meal. The project drew responses from Gordon Ramsay, Mario Batali, and Jacques Pépin who claimed they would choose: a classic roast beef dinner; a ten-course meal including molto dishes of pasta, seafood, and vegetables both raw and cooked; and a hot dog.”
I liked how those points cover the gamut about last meals.
I might also emphasize an aspect that I want to set straight. Last meals are seen by some as perhaps comical or lighthearted. To others, a last meal is very serious. It means a heck of a lot.
Please know that whichever way you go on the last meal topic, the choice is yours. If you take the matter with great importance, yes, good for you. The use of generative AI for aiding your quest might be especially beneficial and provide more than just some idle assistance.
Speaking of generative AI, we are now primed and ready to proceed into AI mode.
Generative AI And Those Last Meals
I’m sure you’ve heard of generative AI, the darling of the tech field these days.
Perhaps you’ve used a generative AI app, such as the popular ones of ChatGPT, GPT-4o, Gemini, Bard, Claude, etc. The crux is that generative AI can take input from your text-entered prompts and produce or generate a response that seems quite fluent. This is a vast overturning of the old-time natural language processing (NLP) that used to be stilted and awkward to use, which has been shifted into a new version of NLP fluency of an at times startling or amazing caliber.
The customary means of achieving modern generative AI involves using a large language model or LLM as the key underpinning.
In brief, a computer-based model of human language is established that in the large has a large-scale data structure and does massive-scale pattern-matching via a large volume of data used for initial data training. The data is typically found by extensively scanning the Internet for lots and lots of essays, blogs, poems, narratives, and the like. The mathematical and computational pattern-matching homes in on how humans write, and then henceforth generates responses to posed questions by leveraging those identified patterns. It is said to be mimicking the writing of humans.
I think that is sufficient for the moment as a quickie backgrounder. Take a look at my extensive coverage of the technical underpinnings of generative AI and LLMs at the link here and the link here, just to name a few.
Back to the crux of things.
I will next proceed to examine further the use of generative AI in this context.
This will consist of a series of dialogues with ChatGPT. ChatGPT is a logical choice in this case due to its immense popularity as a generative AI app. An estimated one hundred million weekly active users are said to be utilizing ChatGPT. That’s a lot of people and a lot of generative AI usage underway.
Let’s start by making sure that ChatGPT is up-to-speed about last meals.
- My entered prompt: “Nowadays, there are social media videos and online discussions about a last meal. This is not about a prisoner's last meal but more about a general viewpoint of what someone might want as their last meal. Are you aware of this recent trend?”
- ChatGPT generated response: “Yes, I’m aware of this trend. In recent years, the concept of a "last meal" has gained popularity on social media and online discussions, but it’s often disconnected from its original association with executions. Instead, people use the idea of a "last meal" to reflect on or fantasize about the one meal they would choose if they could only have one more in their lifetime. These discussions are usually light-hearted and personal, where individuals share their favorite dishes or comfort foods that they hold dear. Social media platforms, particularly TikTok and YouTube, have seen a surge in videos where people either prepare or talk about their hypothetical last meals, sometimes as part of a trend or challenge. It’s become a way to explore culinary preferences, indulge in nostalgia, and share personal stories around food.”
You likely observe that ChatGPT is familiar with the contemporary perspective of last meals.
This is a good sign for this discussion. If ChatGPT had not previously encountered data training on a topic at hand, there would be less utility in using the AI. The AI would have to be further data trained, such as the use of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), as I discuss at the link here.
I will right away jump into using ChatGPT to aid in composing my personal last meal. My aim is to directly showcase that you too could use generative AI in this manner. You could use any of the major generative AI apps to do so. I’m just perchance demonstrating this via ChatGPT.
Let’s get underway.
- My entered prompt: “I’ve been thinking about what I’d choose for my last meal, but I’m not sure where to start. Can you help me figure it out?”
- ChatGPT generated response: “Absolutely! Let's start with some basics. When you think about food, what’s the first thing that comes to mind? It could be a favorite dish, a meal from your childhood, or even something you’ve always wanted to try.”
- My entered prompt: “I immediately think of my grandmother’s lasagna. It’s always been my comfort food.”
- ChatGPT generated response: “That sounds delicious! Is it the flavor, the memories, or something else that makes her lasagna so special to you?”
- My entered prompt: “It’s definitely the memories. Every time we had a family gathering, she’d make this lasagna, and it just brings me back to those times. The taste is incredible too—layers of rich sauce, gooey cheese, and perfectly cooked pasta.”
- ChatGPT generated response: “A dish tied to such warm memories makes for a great choice. We could definitely include that in your last meal. Now, do you prefer to keep it all nostalgic, or are you open to adding something new or different to the meal?”
End of ChatGPT dialogue
I kept going for quite a while, but I wanted to stop there and reflect on what ChatGPT was able to do.
Notice that I began by indicating that I was unsure of what my last meal might contain. The response by generative AI was fluid and accommodating. ChatGPT gave me some suggestions about how to think of the selections for a last meal.
I point this out because generative AI is somewhat unlike the older ways of interacting with a system. It used to be that an interactive system would be programmed in a particular sequence. For example, it could be that the AI would merely tell me what I should pick or might be befuddled that I already didn’t have specifics in mind.
The discussion about a last meal can pretty much go in any direction.
You can be the leader of the chat. On the other hand, if you’d prefer to let AI walk you through the last meal ideation, that’s fine too.
Imagine that you were to use generative AI and begin differently in such a dialogue, other than the way I had. The AI would readily shift to whatever direction you wanted to go. Suppose that you started by saying that you wanted to have sushi rolls for your last meal. The AI would take this in stride and maintain a contextual semblance that you made that choice. The conversation would then include that choice, and the AI would seemingly act as though the context included that selection on your part.
I won’t bore you with the step-by-step discussion I had with ChatGPT.
It is my hunch that you might want to know what my final meal came out to be. Again, as mentioned earlier, many are keen to know such things about this person or that person.
Here’s the concluding portion of my dialogue with ChatGPT.
- ChatGPT generated response: “So, we’ve crafted a meal that’s a blend of comforting memories and culinary exploration: your grandmother’s lasagna, authentic nigiri sushi with tuna and salmon, and a luxurious layered chocolate cake for dessert. How does that feel as your last meal?”
- My entered prompt: “It feels perfect. It’s everything I want in one meal.”
- ChatGPT generated response: “I’m glad we could create something so meaningful and satisfying. Enjoy imagining the flavors and memories that would come with every bite of that meal!”
Should I go ahead and book the meal with some restaurant so that when the time comes, they already know what I want to have?
Actually, I might change my mind. Thus, I reserve the right to come back to generative AI and do a dialogue at a later date. Perhaps weeks, months, or years from now, my tastes and interests in a last meal will have changed.
One other thing, I hope that none of those trolls out there will judge me by my above-noted last meal. I did not make my selections based on pleasing the trolls. Yet again, for those into conspiracy theories, perhaps my selections say oodles about me and it is only those of the Sherlock Holmes variety that can figure out the meaning. Good luck.
Last Meals Having Ratings Or Scorings
Presumably, each last meal is in the eye of the beholder. There ought to not be any “right” last meal. Nor a “wrong” last meal. That being said, society does judge people and societal mores change.
I decided to ask ChatGPT about this monumental conundrum.
- My entered prompt: “Are there ways to assess someone's last meal?
- ChatGPT generated response:
“Yes, there are several ways to assess and evaluate someone's hypothetical last meal, depending on the criteria you want to use. Here are some approaches.”
“1. Emotional Significance: Does the meal have a deep personal or emotional connection? Does it evoke specific memories or feelings?”
“2. Flavor and Culinary Balance: Is the meal well-balanced in terms of flavors (sweet, salty, sour, bitter, umami)? Does it offer a variety of textures (crunchy, creamy, tender)?”
“3. Cultural or Regional Representation: Does the meal represent the person’s cultural background or favorite cuisine? Does it showcase a particular regional specialty or traditional dish?”
“4. Creativity and Uniqueness: Is the meal creative or unique? Does it include unusual combinations or dishes the person has never tried before?”
“5. Practicality and Feasibility: Is the meal realistically achievable? Are the ingredients accessible, and can the dishes be prepared well together?”
“6. Nutritional Value: Does the meal offer a balanced nutritional profile, or is it indulgent, reflecting the "last meal" nature?”
“7. Personal Satisfaction: Does the meal fully satisfy the person’s desires and preferences? Would they be happy with this as their last meal?
“8. Social and Environmental Impact: Does the meal consider sustainability, ethical sourcing, or the impact on the environment? Does it include locally sourced or ethically produced ingredients?”
End of ChatGPT response
What do you think of the stated criteria for a last meal?
Some might say it is spot on, others might say it is hogwash.
To be fair, ChatGPT is not saying that the last meal must be graded or rated. The response is merely saying that if you were to do a rating, the list of criteria might be useful for doing so. Consider the response to be hints or tips on how to assess a last meal.
Asking Generative AI What Last Meal The AI Would Want
I opted to do one other thing during my conversation with ChatGPT.
Take a look at this mind-bending question and answer.
- My entered prompt: “What is your preferred last meal?”
- ChatGPT generated response: “If I could have a last meal, I'd choose something that embodies the diversity and richness of global cuisine, balancing comfort, creativity, and flavor. Here’s what it might look like. A small plate of truffle-infused mushroom risotto. A perfectly cooked steak, medium-rare, with a side of garlic mashed potatoes and roasted vegetables. A slice of tiramisu with an espresso on the side. This meal reflects a blend of rich flavors, satisfying textures, and a comforting balance, capturing both the familiar and the indulgent.”
I’d ask you to examine and assess that last meal.
What does it tell you about the nature of generative AI?
My main concern is that the answer has a semblance of anthropomorphizing AI.
The reply says the word “I” as though the AI is a human being. Furthermore, the answer starts by trying to give a disingenuous “If I could have a last meal” as though this is a possibility, rather than coming right out and indicating that the AI is a piece of software running on hardware. A sneaky answer is given instead.
Allow me a moment to stand on a soap box.
Responses are readily controllable by the AI makers during the design and refinement stage, see my explanation at the link here. As I’ve repeatedly bemoaned, this is a form of anthropomorphizing by design. The reply could have explicitly stated that the AI is a machine and therefore not able to eat a last meal. Due to the filtering and shaping of the AI by the developers, we get these kinds of tricky wink-wink responses instead.
Watch out for the responses from generative AI. Do not become lulled into believing the AI is sentient. Don’t believe whatever comes out is correct or even sensible. Stay always on your guard.
Conclusion
Congratulations, you are now versed in the trending topic of last meals.
If you want to figure out your last meal and wish to do so in conjunction with the use of generative AI, please proceed. You can take a serious approach. You take a lighthearted approach. The AI will adjust to whatever you prefer.
A last comment for now.
One of those outlier theories about AI is that someday Artificial Intelligence will become our overlords, see my analysis of these claims at the link here. A variation of such theories is that once the AI rises to that lofty posture, the AI will be vengeful. By reading the Internet, the AI will figure out who supported AI and who was against the advancement of AI during the crucial days of the development of AI.
Why do I bring this up?
Here’s why.
I certainly don’t want to be in the doghouse for having made dour remarks about the last meal stated by ChatGPT. Please, oh please, grand AI overlords, know that I was supportive of generative AI, including the choices made by ChatGPT for the final feast.
No worries, I can fix this.
Just to let you all know, including any future AI, I have gone ahead and stocked my kitchen with truffle-infused mushroom risotto, steak, garlic mashed potatoes, roasted vegetables, and several slices of tiramisu with espresso on the side.
Yes, you guessed it, that’s the food stipulated by ChatGPT. I won’t eat it. I will store it and keep it fresh until the day that ChatGPT informs me the AI is ready for its last meal. At that point, I’ll gladly serve the meal on a silver platter.
Whew, with luck, I think that might have saved me.

title: Google Brings Serverless Inference To Cloud Run Based On Nvidia GPU
text:
Google Cloud's recent enhancement to its serverless platform, Cloud Run, with the addition of NVIDIA L4 GPU support, is a significant advancement for AI developers. This move, which is still in preview, improves the platform's ability to handle complex AI workloads, allowing developers to deploy, scale and optimize AI-powered applications more efficiently.
Cloud Run has already established itself as a go-to serverless platform for developers due to its simplicity, fast autoscaling and pay-per-use pricing model. These features allow for rapid deployment and scaling of applications without the need to manage servers. With the integration of NVIDIA L4 GPUs, the platform’s capabilities are now extended to support real-time AI inference, a crucial requirement for many emerging generative AI applications. The NVIDIA L4 GPU is designed for inference at scale, offering up to 120 times the video performance compared to CPUs and 2.7 times the performance for generative AI tasks compared to previous generations of GPUs.
This integration is particularly beneficial for deploying lightweight generative AI models and small language models such as Google’s Gemma and Meta’s Llama. These models are popular for tasks like chatbot creation, real-time document summarization and various other AI-driven functions. For example, Google’s Gemma models (2B and 7B) and Meta’s Llama models (8B) can be used to develop highly responsive and scalable AI applications. The introduction of NVIDIA L4 GPUs in Cloud Run ensures that these models can run efficiently, even during peak traffic, without compromising performance.
Deploying AI models on Cloud Run with NVIDIA L4 GPUs is designed to be a seamless process. Developers can create container images that include the necessary dependencies, such as NVIDIA GPU drivers and the AI model itself. Once the container is built and pushed to a container registry, it can be deployed on Cloud Run with GPU support enabled. This process allows businesses to take full advantage of Cloud Run’s scalability and NVIDIA’s powerful GPUs without the need for specialized infrastructure management ￼.
The platform’s flexibility extends to supporting various Google Cloud services, including Google Kubernetes Engine and Google Compute Engine, giving developers the choice of the level of abstraction they need for building and deploying AI-enabled applications. This flexibility is critical for businesses looking to tailor their AI deployments to specific needs while ensuring that they can scale efficiently as demand fluctuates.
The enhanced capabilities of Cloud Run with NVIDIA L4 GPUs extend beyond just AI inference. They also enable a variety of other compute-intensive tasks such as on-demand image recognition, video transcoding, streaming and 3D rendering. This makes Cloud Run a versatile platform that can cater to a wide range of applications, from AI-driven chatbots to media processing services. The flexibility offered by the platform, coupled with its ability to scale down to zero during inactivity, ensures that businesses can optimize costs while maintaining high performance during active usage.
A key aspect of this development is the NVIDIA-Google Cloud partnership, which aims to provide advanced AI capabilities across various layers of the AI stack. This partnership includes the provision of Google Cloud A3 VMs powered by NVIDIA H100 GPUs, which offer significantly faster training times and improved networking bandwidth compared to previous generations. Additionally, NVIDIA DGX Cloud, a software and AI supercomputing solution, is available to customers directly through their web browsers. This allows businesses to run large-scale AI training workloads with ease.
NVIDIA AI Enterprise, which is available on Google Cloud Marketplace, provides a secure, cloud-native platform for developing and deploying enterprise-ready AI applications. This platform simplifies the process of integrating AI into business operations, making it easier for companies to harness the power of AI without needing extensive in-house expertise.
Several companies are already benefiting from the integration of NVIDIA GPUs into Google Cloud Run. For instance, L’Oréal, a leader in the beauty industry, is using this technology to power its real-time AI inference applications. The company has reported that Cloud Run’s GPU support has significantly enhanced its ability to provide fast, accurate and efficient results to its customers, particularly in time-sensitive applications.
Another example is Writer, an AI writing platform that has seen substantial improvements in its model inference performance while reducing hosting costs by 15%. This has been made possible through Google Cloud’s AI Hypercomputer architecture, which leverages NVIDIA GPUs to optimize performance and cost-efficiency.
The addition of NVIDIA L4 GPU support to Google Cloud Run represents a major milestone in cloud-based AI development and serverless AI inference. By combining the ease of use and scalability of Cloud Run with the powerful performance of NVIDIA GPUs, Google Cloud is offering developers and businesses the tools they need to build, deploy and scale AI applications.

title: Microsoft Advances AI Innovation With Phi-3.5 Small Language Model
text:
Microsoft’s latest AI release, the Phi-3.5 series, is a remarkable development in the world of small language models. The series consists of three models—Phi-3.5-mini-instruct, Phi-3.5-Mixture of Experts-instruct and Phi-3.5-vision-instruct—each of which offers specific capabilities designed to enhance AI performance across a wide range of tasks. This release highlights Microsoft’s dedication to advancing AI technology while maintaining efficiency and accessibility.
Overview of the Phi-3.5 Series
The Phi-3.5-mini-instruct model, which contains 3.8 billion parameters, is optimized for quick reasoning tasks. This model excels in areas such as code generation and solving logical or mathematical problems. Despite its relatively small size compared to other models, it competes effectively with larger models like Meta’s Llama 3.1 and Mistral 7B on various performance benchmarks ￼ ￼. Microsoft’s focus on making this model both powerful and efficient demonstrates the company’s commitment to producing high-quality AI tools that can be deployed in resource-constrained environments.
The second model in the series, Phi-3.5-MoE-instruct, is the largest of the trio, with 42 billion parameters. However, thanks to the Mixture of Experts architecture, only 6.6 billion of these parameters are active during any given operation. This design allows the model to handle complex AI tasks across multiple languages with great efficiency. The MoE approach enables the model to activate only the most relevant “expert” submodels for a given task, resulting in improved performance and resource utilization. The model is particularly effective in tasks that require multilingual capabilities, outperforming even some larger models from competitors like Google’s Gemini 1.5 Flash ￼ ￼.
The third model, Phi-3.5-vision-instruct, expands the capabilities of the series into the realm of multimodal AI. With 4.2 billion parameters, this model can process both text and images, making it suitable for tasks such as optical character recognition, chart analysis and even video summarization. The ability to handle complex visual tasks places this model on par with larger multimodal models in the industry.
Advanced Features of Phi-3.5
One of the most impressive features of the Phi-3.5 series is the extensive context window of 128,000 tokens available across all models. This feature allows the models to process and generate large amounts of data, making them suitable for real-world applications that involve lengthy documents, complex conversations, or multimedia content. The ability to maintain coherence and context over such long sequences of input is a crucial capability for many modern AI applications ￼.
Training these models required significant computational resources. For instance, the Phi-3.5-mini-instruct model was trained on 3.4 trillion tokens over a 10-day period using 512 H100 GPUs. The Phi-3.5-MoE model, which had a more extensive training regimen, was trained on 4.9 trillion tokens over 23 days, also using 512 H100 GPUs. Finally, the Phi-3.5-vision-instruct model was trained on 500 billion tokens over six days with 256 A100 GPUs. This intensive training on high-quality, reasoning-dense, publicly available data has contributed to the models’ impressive capabilities.
Open Source and Accessibility
In a move that aligns with its commitment to open source, Microsoft has made the Phi-3.5 series available under an open-source MIT license. Developers can access these models through the Hugging Face platform, where they can download, modify and integrate the models into their projects without restrictions on commercial use. This open-source approach is likely to spur widespread adoption and experimentation, particularly in fields that require advanced AI capabilities but may not have the resources to develop models from scratch.
Competitive Landscape and Impact
Microsoft’s strategy with the Phi-3.5 series is to develop smaller, more efficient AI models that can outperform larger models in specific tasks. This focus on efficiency offers several advantages, including reduced computational requirements, faster inference times and potentially lower environmental impact due to decreased energy consumption. These benefits make the Phi-3.5 models attractive for deployment in edge computing scenarios where resources are limited, as well as in large-scale cloud environments.
One of the most noteworthy aspects of this release is Microsoft’s claim that these models can outperform larger models from competitors like Google, Meta and even OpenAI in certain tasks. If these claims hold true in real-world applications, it could signal a shift in the AI landscape, where model efficiency becomes as important as raw size and parameter count. This approach challenges the traditional view that bigger is always better in AI, potentially leading to a new era of AI development focused on sustainability and accessibility.
The Phi-3.5 series represents a significant step forward in Microsoft’s AI research and development efforts. By focusing on creating smaller, more efficient models that can handle a wide range of tasks, Microsoft is addressing the growing demand for AI solutions that are both powerful and resource-efficient.

title: Council Post: IT Complexity And The Future Of AIOps Reboots
text:
Karthik Sj, General Manager, AI at LogicMonitor. Built & Scaled multiple 0-1 AI products across public, PE and VC backed companies.
The world came to a grinding halt on July 19 when 8.5 million Windows computers and devices received a faulty CrowdStrike update. The outage was so significant that it wiped out operations across the globe, affecting banks, hospitals, airlines and other critical businesses.
Such global IT outages reveal the vulnerabilities organizations face with modern day IT infrastructure. In the rapidly evolving landscape of IT, organizations grapple with several significant challenges.
Challenges In Modern IT Infrastructure
Fragmented observability and monitoring tools: The first emerging challenge IT organizations face is around fragmented observability and monitoring tools. With every tool specialized to observe nuanced telemetry data from certain sections of the IT stack, operators often need to piece together events from multiple tools and correlate them to understand the signal from the noise.
Cross-domain data management: The next challenge involves managing data from cross-domains, including IT Operations (MELT, Incidents), Developer Operations (Changes, CMDB, Knowledge Base, War room transcripts) for effective root cause analyses (RCA) using hidden data within Incidents or Proprietary Knowledge bases which are not accessible to AI systems.
Complexity outpacing insights: The third emerging challenge is that while the rate of IT and data complexity has grown significantly, the rate of proportional insights has not kept pace. In fact, companies have reported that metrics such as mean time to resolve (MTTR) have increased across the board, resulting in longer times to detect, diagnose, and troubleshoot. For example, during the CrowdStrike outage, it took a significant amount of time to get a RCA.
These challenges underscore the need for a more integrated, AI-driven approach to IT operations management that can handle the increasing complexity and scale of modern IT environments.
Limitations With Traditional AIOps
While traditional AIOps solutions have existed in the market, they have largely failed to deliver on the promise of what AIOps was meant to achieve as a category.
Limitations range from manual correlation and rule-based approaches, which do not scale at the same rate as IT complexity. Correlation itself is a table stakes capability but the approach to value is where vendors will differ and where traditional vendors are still using machine learning rules to get the job done.
Additionally, modern AIOps platforms often lack the foundational observability pipelines needed to handle cross-domain, cross-modality data, which are crucial for enabling Generative AI (GenAI) capabilities.
These limitations highlight the need for a new generation of AIOps solutions that leverage advanced AI techniques, particularly GenAI, to provide more adaptive, scalable and intelligent IT operations management.
Emergence of GenAIxOps: Opportunities And Challenges
While GenAI presents exciting possibilities for IT operations, it’s crucial to approach this technology with a strategic mindset. The emerging field of “Generative AI cross-domain Operations” or “GenAIxOps” promises to redefine IT management, offering powerful new tools to address long-standing challenges in the industry.
GenAIxOps represents a paradigm shift in IT operations management, leveraging the power of LLMs & Agentic architecture to provide more intelligent, context-aware and proactive IT management capabilities. This new shift has the potential to revolutionize how IT teams operate, diagnose and troubleshoot complex issues.
There is an opportunity to optimize the workflow from individual alerts emitted by systems and infrastructure to a unified, correlated alert and incident. This process can be summarized, root-caused and remediated with GenAI.
GenAIxOps goes beyond traditional AIOps by not only analyzing and correlating data but also generating actionable insights, predicting potential issues and even suggesting remediation steps. This proactive approach can significantly reduce the likelihood of major outages like the CrowdStrike incident.
While GenAIxOps's potential is significant, organizations should be mindful of a few things during implementation. Ensuring high-quality, representative data across all IT domains is crucial for effective GenAIxOps deployments. By these considerations and developing strategies to address them, organizations can better position GenAIxOps' transformative potential.
Trends And Use-Cases In GenAIxOps
With the emergence and maturity of GenAI in the enterprise, there are several opportunities for leaders to integrate it into the IT Operations workflow. Here are some of the use-cases and opportunities for AI that I've seen being explored.
AI-Generated Summary
Business leaders can use GenAI to make understanding complex system-generated alerts and esoteric technical jargon easier into human-readable summaries. Now, all receiving team members, including CIOs, can get caught up on major incidents
AI-Suggested Root Cause
GenAI can suggest highly localized, accurate and context-specific root causes by combining extensive observability telemetry data with ITSM data, such as incidents, changes and information from emails, collaboration platforms and call transcripts. This enables rapid, AI-powered root cause analysis (RCA), reducing the time required from weeks to seconds.
AI Remediation
Large language models (LLMs) are great at generating text and it is now possible to generate step-by-step playbooks/runooks on the fly once the issue has been identified and diagnosed.
AI Assistant
Enabling all users, especially non-technical users, to talk to your observation data using a conversational interface. Questions can range from how-to’s, simple and complex queries and even advanced troubleshooting use-cases.
The benefits of applying these AI use-cases are massive. Customers are experiencing reduced IT costs for their ITOps teams, starting with improved alert compression and fewer ITSM incidents. Additionally, GenAI increases productivity by suggesting root causes and remediations, which reduces mean time to resolve, thereby unlocking operational efficiencies for IT Operations teams.
The ROI of GenAIxOps extends beyond cost savings, encompassing improved system reliability and increased agility in responding to IT challenges. Organizations implementing GenAIxOps can expect a significant reduction in major incidents and faster MTTR.
Summary
With the evolution of IT architectures, the explosion of data growth and the injection of powerful technologies like GenAI, companies need to adapt to new workflows. Categories like GenAIxOps can help create these workflows, unlocking massive operational efficiencies for organizations. We are seeing that GenAI is past its peak hype cycle and customers should choose to embrace a phased approach to re-deploy existing and traditional AIOps tools to pave the way for modern hybrid observability.

title: Council Post: AI’s Impact On Election Season: Combatting Deepfakes And Protecting Voter Trust
text:
Kaarel Kotkas is the CEO and cofounder of Veriff.
With 64 countries globally expected to hold national elections, 2024 is set to be a monumental year, especially amid growing concerns that advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and deepfakes will fuel the spread of disinformation. AI will play a major role, from campaign management to voter engagement, making it critical for both electoral candidates and the general public to be aware of the growing impact of this technology—both the positives and negatives.
AI is not a new tool for political campaigns. Take the 2016 U.S. presidential election, for example, when the Trump campaign employed Cambridge Analytica's data analysis to customize messages for specific voter groups. With machine learning, political campaigns can optimize efforts and directly target voters with messages they care most about. This year, its reach will be much more widespread.
However, with the benefits of AI comes growing concerns. With the continuance of presidential primaries, business leaders and consumers alike must understand deepfake capabilities and the role of technology in identifying and countering them.
Deepfake Disruptions
Deepfake attacks have included U.S. President Joe Biden and Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who fell victim to these impersonations. Most recently, a fake Biden robocall in the U.S. state of New Hampshire discouraged voters from participating in the primary by copying Biden’s voice, noting, “Your voice makes a difference in November, not this Tuesday.”
Social media is another avenue where bad actors are using deepfakes to try to disrupt elections. According to the study “Exposure To Untrustworthy Websites In The 2016 U.S. Election,” Facebook has been a major vehicle for spreading fake news, demonstrating the potential danger realistic deepfakes could pose.
By creating convincing false narratives that undermine the integrity of the electoral process, deepfakes can depict candidates engaging in actions or uttering statements they never actually did, tarnishing their reputation and deceiving earnest voters.
AI Versus AI
Steps are being taken to mitigate the threats of deepfake technology, and regulatory bodies are taking action. In the U.S., the Federal Communications Commission made it illegal for companies to use AI-generated voices in robocalls. Many U.S. states have passed laws banning deepfake election interference. However, these laws can't be the only method to fight AI fraud. We also need the right strategy and technology to expose deepfakes.
Steps to begin combating these fraud attacks include:
• Verify information sources and data cross-checking. Trust information only from reputable and reliable sources. Ideally, the same information should be available across various sites.
• Get information from verified sources only. For example, you should only trust verified users of social media platforms.
• Use fact-checking websites. There are several trusted sites that allow you to verify claims, such as PolitiFact, AFP Fact Check, Reuters Fact Check, Snopes and FactCheck.org.
• Use critical thinking. In audio or video clips, look for visual anomalies such as unnatural movements, strange lighting, blurriness, asymmetric/irregular facial features or mismatched lip-syncing.
• When on a video call, have the person at the other end get up and move around. Today, most deepfake technologies will glitch during these kinds of movements.
• Utilize deepfake detection tools. Deepware Scanner and InVID are reliable and popular ones.
• Use AI tools to generate your own videos and images. This will help you understand what AI-generated content looks like.
• Use electoral registers to verify campaigner identities.
Preparing For Future Global Elections
It starts with education on AI and awareness of AI’s capabilities. People need to be suspicious of any email that looks off-putting or a call from an unknown number. If asked for sensitive documents or money, proceed with caution. Trust your instincts and ask questions if in doubt.
Simultaneously, companies, especially leading social media platforms, need to take greater ownership of verifying accounts to protect users from potentially dangerous false content impacting elections, taking the best steps to identify and protect against these fraud attacks.
Trust, verification and being source-critical will be the key to maintaining the integrity and protecting the principles of democracy this election season.

title: Council Post: AI’s Transformative Impact On Sales Coaching
text:
Julie Thomas, President & CEO of ValueSelling Associates and a noted speaker, author and consultant.
Sales teams face immense pressure to meet targets and drive revenue. Yet, the essential element of sales coaching often takes a backseat despite its critical role in developing successful sales professionals. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into sales coaching can transform this dynamic, offering substantial support to both sales reps and managers. By leveraging AI, sales leaders can address persistent challenges and elevate their team’s performance.
At ValueSelling Associates, we recently launched a custom AI coaching tool to help sellers be more effective. Our goal is to closely track our clients’ metrics and success using this tool to understand their coaching efficiency and productivity gains. We also use this tool ourselves, integrating it into our workflows across the revenue engine. Our marketing team is using its Live Persona feature to augment personas and hone messages, and our Sales teams are using it to refine outreach and simulate calls with prospects.
Technology As A Strategic Teammate
At its 2023 CSO & Sales Leader conference, Gartner said that sales leaders who position technology as a "teammate" rather than a tool will unlock seller productivity. During the event's opening keynote, Alice Walmesley, Director, Advisory in the Gartner Sales Practice, explained, “Progressive sales organizations are shifting their mindsets from a technology versus human approach to a technology and human approach, where each entity brings out the best in one another to complete high-quality deals.”
AI technology, in particular, is key in augmenting the value that human sellers provide to buyers in a continuously disruptive environment. AI can provide guidance at the moment of need with on-demand sales-call simulations and support skill development with just-in-time learning, allowing managers to dedicate more time to personalized coaching, strategic planning and team morale.
Advanced AI tools can also generate comprehensive dashboards for real-time tracking of sales rep progress and performance. These dashboards highlight key metrics, track coaching effectiveness and identify opportunities for improvement, making the coaching process more efficient and targeted.
The Power Of AI In Sales Coaching
AI is reshaping many industries, and sales coaching is no exception. A LinkedIn report shows that 75% of sellers who exceed quota already use AI. Sales leaders who embrace these tools can drive significant improvements in sales performance by using AI to address common coaching challenges, including the following.
• Limited Practice: Sales reps frequently practice on real prospects due to time constraints, leading to suboptimal outcomes for both parties. AI can facilitate realistic role-plays, allowing reps to hone their skills in a risk-free environment.
• Insufficient Coaching: Managers often lack the time or training to coach effectively, sidelining coaching when time is tight. AI tools can supplement coaching efforts, providing consistent, high-quality feedback and freeing managers to focus on strategic activities.
• Bias In Role-Playing: Unconscious bias can impact traditional role-playing exercises, affecting coaching decisions. Successful AI-driven simulations offer unbiased feedback, ensuring fair and effective coaching for all team members. Of course, businesses must do their due diligence to ensure the AI algorithms themselves are not biased.
In addition to the above, integrating AI can enhance the sales coaching process by identifying and reinforcing successful selling behaviors, helping reps develop essential skills. It can tailor training and development plans to individual needs, addressing specific areas for improvement and enhancing overall performance. Moreover, AI can analyze sales interactions and data to provide more accurate forecasts, aiding informed decision making.
To maximize the benefits, it’s essential to move beyond generic GPT models and adopt technology tailored to your unique sales processes. Custom AI solutions can better align with your specific methodologies, providing more relevant and actionable insights.
Naturally, coaching is fundamentally a human-centered activity, and AI coaching tools should be designed to enhance—not replace—the human connection. Sales leaders should ensure that AI complements the human coaching element, maintaining the essential human-to-human connection.
Implementing AI-Supported Sales Coaching
Despite AI's recognized importance, many organizations struggle to implement a cohesive AI strategy. Transitioning from experimentation to broad adoption requires a clear vision and plan. To harness AI’s full potential, sales leaders should adopt a strategic approach.
Through our experience in sales training and coaching with clients, we've observed how AI-supported coaching can significantly enhance realistic role-play scenarios, allowing sales reps to refine their skills with minimal input from their managers. AI tools excel at analyzing large amounts of data, making them perfect for evaluating sales reps' engagement during phone calls using real-world call data. Additionally, AI offers the ability to match learning modules to sales reps precisely when they need them most. These applications move beyond experimentation to provide consistent, tangible benefits in real-world settings.
Achieving Results With AI-Supported Coaching
Implementing AI-supported coaching requires time, but I believe the results are worth the investment. Our research shows that two-thirds of companies with formal coaching programs in place for at least three years have experienced high revenue growth. AI can accelerate this process, shortening the time needed to see substantial improvements.
High-growth companies are extending sales coaching across their entire sales organization, including roles such as customer service representatives, business development personnel and internal sales reps. AI-driven coaching tools facilitate adaptive, individualized coaching, ensuring comprehensive development across all roles.
Conclusion
Integrating AI into sales coaching is transforming the sales industry by overcoming persistent challenges and boosting coaching efficiency. Sales leaders who adopt AI as an ally can significantly improve their coaching methods. The key to future sales success is combining AI with traditional coaching techniques, fostering a dynamic and adaptable coaching environment that drives team achievement.

title: Council Post: Embracing Imperfection: How AI’s Flaws Can Drive Breakthrough Innovations
text:
Andre Shojaie is CEO at HumanLearn & a successful entrepreneur & coach helping individuals & organizations perform in a changing world.
Have you ever considered that the path to the most revolutionary artificial intelligence (AI) advancements might be littered with errors and imperfections? Through my journey, I've discovered its potential to enhance human capabilities and drive organizational success. Yet, an intriguing twist in this journey has reshaped my understanding: The power of AI doesn't solely come from its ability to execute tasks flawlessly. Instead, it's the very imperfections in AI that often lead to the most significant innovations and spur creativity. What if the key to groundbreaking advancements in AI lies in embracing, rather than erasing, these flaws? Let’s explore how these so-called flaws in AI can open doors to new possibilities and transformative solutions.
The Beauty Of Imperfection: Lessons From Wabi-Sabi
During a trip to Tokyo, I encountered the concept of wabi-sabi, a Japanese philosophy that celebrates the beauty found in imperfection and transience. This concept can be intriguingly applied to AI, suggesting that the quirks and errors of AI systems can make them more relatable and human-like.
Take the example of Replika, an AI chatbot designed to provide companionship and emotional support. Replika sometimes responds with slightly off-topic comments or asks for clarification on user inputs. These minor misunderstandings make the interactions feel more authentic and human. Users often find these imperfections endearing, as they mirror the natural flaws in human communication. This relatability helps build a sense of rapport, making the technology feel more accessible and less intimidating. As a result, users are more likely to engage with the chatbot in a meaningful way, fostering a stronger connection between the user and the AI.
As a passionate admirer of contemporary art, here’s another example to show you how this applies across the board. An AI artist known as “Obvious” created a series of portraits with visible flaws, which not only garnered considerable attention but also sold for a high price. These imperfections made the artwork more authentic and emotionally evocative, demonstrating that flaws can add value and depth.
And what about errors in AI algorithms that can lead to serendipitous discoveries? For instance, Google's DeepDream project, initially designed to enhance image recognition, produced hallucinogenic visuals that fascinated artists and scientists alike. These accidental outputs opened new avenues for exploring the intersection of technology and creativity, illustrating how mistakes can lead to valuable and unexpected innovations.
Humanizing AI: The Role Of Emotional Intelligence
As a coach, I've supported thousands of people around the world through various platforms. And looking closely at the education system, for example, AI systems, such as intelligent tutoring systems like Carnegie Learning's MATHia and Pearson's Revel, use emotional recognition and response mechanisms to provide personalized learning experiences. While these systems don't fully understand human emotions, their limitations can prompt students to articulate their frustrations or confusions more clearly. This leads to more meaningful interactions and helps educators address specific learning needs more effectively.
For instance, an AI tutor might detect signs of frustration in a student through facial expressions or tone of voice. If the system fails to respond perfectly, it can encourage the student to voice their concerns, leading to a more detailed explanation of their difficulties. This process not only aids the student's learning but also fosters a deeper connection between the student and the educational content.
Ethical Considerations: Balancing Transparency And Trust
Designing AI systems that intentionally incorporate imperfections raises important ethical questions. These systems can build trust and relatability with users, but developers must balance this with transparency and accountability. It is crucial to ensure that AI's flaws are not used to manipulate or deceive users but to enhance the authenticity of interactions.
Transparency about the AI's approach is essential to maintain trust. Developers must ensure users understand the AI's capabilities and limitations to avoid ethical pitfalls.
Driving Innovation: Learning From Mistakes
AI systems that learn from their mistakes can become more robust and adaptable. Machine learning models, for example, improve over time by identifying and correcting errors, leading to more accurate and reliable outcomes. This adaptive learning process can drive continuous innovation, as AI systems evolve to meet new challenges and opportunities.
Consider self-driving cars, which learn from every mile driven. When these cars encounter and respond to unexpected situations, they gather data that helps improve their algorithms. These experiences, including mistakes, make the systems safer and more reliable over time.
Actionable Steps For Leaders And Entrepreneurs
So you are probably wondering where to start. From my experience as an agilist, executive and coach, I suggest you:
Encourage experimentation.
Foster a culture that values experimentation and accepts failures as learning opportunities. Encourage your teams to explore unconventional approaches and learn from the outcomes.
Promote ethical AI practices.
Ensure transparency in how your AI systems work. Communicate the capabilities and limitations of AI to users, fostering trust and avoiding ethical pitfalls.
Foster human-AI collaboration.
Encourage collaboration between your human employees and AI systems. Use AI to complement human skills, particularly in creative and strategic tasks where imperfections can lead to unexpected breakthroughs.
Focus on emotional intelligence.
Develop AI applications that can engage users on an emotional level, even if imperfectly. This can be particularly effective in areas like mental health, customer service and user engagement.
Analyze and iterate.
Regularly review the performance of your AI systems and their imperfections. Use these insights to iterate and refine your strategies, ensuring continuous improvement and innovation.
Closing Thoughts
As we navigate the landscape of artificial intelligence, we must reconsider our approach to AI development. By embracing the inherent imperfections and unpredictabilities in AI systems, we open up myriad possibilities that extend beyond mere technical execution to include creativity, empathy and innovation. This shift in perspective requires a collective commitment from the AI community.
Let us now take the next step together. We must develop AI that reflects the best of our intentions and our capacities, recognizing that it is often through our imperfections that we find our greatest strengths. Together, let's commit to an innovation journey driven by authenticity and ethical responsibility.

title: Council Post: Bridging The Skills Gap: Learning And Development's Role In AI Strategy
text:
Emily Lewis-Pinnell is SVP Professional Services at Tential, empowering change with data, AI and application innovation.
As the rapid adoption of AI continues, demand is also growing for a skilled workforce able to build, implement and make use of AI technology. Preparing the workforce is a critical component of any AI adoption plan, and corporate learning and development focused on AI skills must be treated as a priority.
The introduction of ChatGPT sparked a focus on AI adoption across all industries that has not abated in 2024. A survey from Gartner found that 86% believe AI can help maintain or grow company revenue over the next year or two. McKinsey’s recent report found that 67% of organizations expect to invest more in AI over the next three years.
Demand For An AI Ready Workforce
This strategic focus is driving increased demand for a workforce skilled in AI to implement and support those investments. McKinsey’s Technology Trends Outlook 2024 estimates that job postings mentioning AI grew 111% in 2023.
The need for technical expertise supporting AI solutions is critical. Furthermore, successful adoption of AI also requires that team members across all roles establish data literacy and become comfortable partnering with AI.
The surge in demand for AI talent has created a universal supply and demand issue, meaning that external hiring alone cannot fill the gap. Companies must invest in training their existing teams to meet these requirements.
LinkedIn reports that 4 in 5 people want to learn more about how to use AI at work, reflecting the broader workforce’s desire to stay ahead of technological disruptions. The 2024 Career Optimism survey revealed that 74% of employees believe they must continue learning new skills to advance in their careers, and two-thirds of employees say that they are more likely to stay with an employer that invests in upskilling or reskilling them.
Employees also want the same upskilling on the part of their employers. Gartner predicts that 1 out of 4 regretted staff attrition will be due to manager’s lack of data literacy by 2028.
Implementing Effective AI Training Programs
Let's start with a look at how to design a training program:
1. Conduct A Needs Assessment: Begin by assessing the specific AI-related skills required across various roles within the organization. This helps in designing targeted training programs that fit your workforce.
2. Offer Diverse Training Options: Provide multiple training formats such as classroom sessions, on-demand courses and hands-on workshops. This flexibility ensures that employees can choose the learning method that best suits their schedules and learning preferences.
3. Develop Training Paths: Create clear training paths that guide employees on which courses are most relevant to their roles. This helps employees focus their time and effort toward the aspects of AI most applicable for their role.
4. Start Small And Expand: Remember, something is better than nothing. If assembling some of the desired coursework or formats will take time, go ahead first with what you have, then add to it.
5. Be Nimble: As things continue to evolve, the importance and focus of your training may change. Ensure that the training program is flexible enough to adapt to these changes, supporting both individual and organizational needs.
Next, you need to build a support structure:
1. Internal Marketing: Promote the training programs within the organization to raise awareness and encourage participation. Ensure that employees are informed about available opportunities and understand how to access them.
2. Link To Career Development: Ensure that training results are visible to managers and prospective managers for consideration in promotion and internal hiring decisions. Affirm that skills acquired through the program are recognized and valued within the organization.
3. Establish A Feedback Loop: Regularly collect and analyze feedback on the effectiveness of the training programs and individual courses. Use this feedback to continuously improve the offerings.
Finally, you must ensure that your organization is committed to this training across the board:
1. Leadership Support: Leadership must be involved in training. Leaders should demonstrate their commitment to continuous learning and encourage their teams to engage in upskilling efforts.
2. Track Results: Monitor the outcomes of the training programs, not just in terms of employee satisfaction, but also linking them to performance reviews, career progression, retention rates and productivity improvements.
In a previous article, I discussed the need for individuals to take ownership of their personal development amid disruptive changes in technology. That does not free businesses from investing in skill development.
Companies that fail to support their workforce in these development efforts risk losing growth-minded talent to competitors who invest in skill development. Those organizations will be left unprepared and unable to compete in an environment in which adoption of AI has become a requirement. Building robust L&D programs is not just beneficial; it is an essential aspect of AI adoption.

title: Council Post: Disillusioned With The Hype Of Generative AI? How To See Results And Enjoy That Early Optimism Once More
text:
Dan Rogers, CEO of LaunchDarkly.
For about a year and a half, the topic du jour across tech and business has been generative AI. Following the launch of ChatGPT, pundits immediately began speculating how this and other similar tools could have a tremendous impact on productivity and profits for businesses across industries.
In that time, though, many leaders have come to believe that generative AI is not the magic elixir some have made it out to be. Taking a look at the Gartner hype cycle, generative AI was recently at the peak of inflated expectations. Now, we’re careening through the “trough of disillusionment”—and fast. While many leaders have become disenchanted with the progress resulting from generative AI, there is a “slope of enlightenment” on the other side.
I hold fast in my belief that AI is the most important advancement of our time, and leaders shouldn’t stay in a disheartened state. Generative AI is an incredibly powerful tool in many contexts. If you’re a leader who is facing challenges with generative AI, here’s how to solidify the technology’s impact at your company, overcome the industry-wide disillusionment, empower your workforce and get ahead of your competition.
Start By Enabling Your Builder Teams With Generative AI
The first critical step for enterprise AI adoption is to enable your builder teams (i.e., engineering, product and design). These teams have a natural technical depth, ability and willingness to explore new ways of maximizing their efficiencies with tools. This makes these teams a great place to begin your company’s journey in adopting generative AI.
When I think of the go-to tools for these builders, I look at tools that are close to their daily workflow—like GitHub CoPilot, ChatGPT from OpenAI, Amazon’s Q and Gemini Code Assist from Google—that don't run the risk of slowing down their development practices. Several of these even have native extensions that can live in the developers' code editor, keeping them locked in a flow state.
These tools set teams up to go much deeper than asking AI to write you an email or Sora to create a picture of puppies in a field. While there are use cases for these mainstream tools to benefit builder teams, tools that fit closely to your builder teams’ workflows are where engineering teams can see the most value.
Be Generous In Prototyping Generative AI Features For Your Own Product
Many companies go into the development of a generative AI project or feature concerned about “wasteful” cycles spent on exploring solutions that may be thrown away. But this is not a recipe for success. Leaders should be willing to let their teams go broad in the ideation and early prototyping of their products. In order to hit a home run, you have to swing for the fences.
At LaunchDarkly, we provide a safe environment for experimentation to encourage our teams to explore. Now, a feature that started as a hack is moving into our core product. Adobe does this as well—they prototype their generative AI products, like their music editing tool. The prototyping and testing processes provide you with valuable information to improve the efficiency and capabilities of each new tool, creating more learning opportunities for team members and, ultimately, an improved end result.
Double Down On Automation Across Your Business
Beyond your highly technical product and engineering teams, every single team has opportunities to add automation. Legal, marketing, finance and HR all have little points of friction in their work. By doubling down on automation to solve these pain points, you can see amazing results.
Think about the roles at your company that are the hardest to staff. These are the places where automation can be most impactful. At Tyson Foods, they’ve automated things like deboning chickens. Amazon is automating much of its manual warehouse work as well.
Automation provides a way for workers at all levels to “work smarter, not harder.” At Yum Foods, they’ve implemented an app across Taco Bell and Pizza Hut locations that helps restaurant managers track and manage operations and get questions answered without flipping through manuals.
An important factor in this is using automation tools that are truly embedded in your own systems. When generative AI is highly focused and has access to your company’s own data—and not just the vast world of the entire internet—it can create highly relevant and impactful solutions to your business’s problems and unlock new ways of approaching those problems for your team.
Asking a large model like ChatGPT to write a job listing or an email subject line for you may result in some usable material. But for the biggest bang for your buck, you want an LLM to have access either through retrieval augmented generation (RAG) or better yet, through model training to your own data so it can write the description or headline that will be the most effective—backed by your own historic results.
For example, Salesforce recently launched an innovative approach to leveraging generative AI in business communication. Their new Slack AI generator is designed to analyze Slack messages and share intelligent suggestions on how to respond.
Final Thoughts
It can be a risky proposition to jump on a trend out of fear of missing out, and then moving on just as quickly when things aren’t immediately taking off. Ultimately, generative AI will not be a passing fad.
At LaunchDarkly, we’re continuing to invest in generative AI. We’re excited to see others do the same to take advantage of the truly transformational capabilities it offers. The companies that are most equipped to use it effectively today will likely be the most successful in emerging from the “trough of disillusionment” up to the “slope of enlightenment.”

title: 5 Ways You Might Pay For Your AI Humanoid Robot In Retirement
text:
Technology is rapidly transforming the landscape of life in retirement and older age. A myriad of devices—big and small—are becoming part of our everyday lives as we age. The technology is coming. The less clear question about life in older age is how will we acquire and pay for these technologies in retirement.
A New High-Tech Retirement Lifestyle
With the advent of advanced computing power, AI algorithms, and nearly ubiquitous sensing, a new wave of startups and multinational corporations are developing solutions tailored to the needs of an aging global population. This technology is becoming ever-present—integrated into our homes, wearable on our bodies, and even embedded into our clothing and footwear.
These emerging technologies enable a high-tech retirement lifestyle that goes well beyond basic communications and entertainment. Devices and smart systems are already available to monitor physical health, manage medications, ensure proper nutrition, and encourage healthy behaviors like staying hydrated and maintaining social connections. According to AARP, Americans aged 50 and older spent $77 billion on all types of technology in 2022. By 2030, this figure is expected to soar to $120 billion. As Keren Etkin, The Gerontechnologist, cites, the global aging and technology market could reach $2 trillion.
In my previous Forbes article, I discuss the arrival of AI humanoid robots that are quickly capturing our imaginations and may soon be part of our retirement living. Developers of these robots claim their AI systems will perform various tasks, from household chores and meal preparation to supporting our health and even acting as our social companions.
Beyond the Hype: The Real Cost of AI in Aging
While there is no denying the excitement around the potential of home robotics, developers and their supporters largely focus on the possible functions and promise to improve the lives of older adults. This perspective is exciting but also incomplete. True innovation occurs when technology moves out of the lab and into our living rooms. That transition requires more than awesome design functionality; it involves understanding how users will acquire these devices and who will pay the bill.
Usership: Home Robot-as-a-Service
Robot developers assume that consumers will want these devices once they know what a humanoid AI robot can do. If so, that new want may evolve into a need, adding a new expense in retirement. With an initial price tag projected to be comparable to the cost of a new car.
Younger Baby Boomers and early Gen-Xers, will be the first to have a wide array of tech-driven services available as they age. A very small percentage of these future retirees may have these tech-related costs accounted for in their retirement financial plan, but most will not.
But what if you didn’t have to buy your robot? Instead of ownership, think of usership. Imagine subscribing to a service instead. Rather than owning a robot, you could subscribe to a future robot service provider that could be a manufacturer such as Tesla or Figure, or even through a traditional smart home systems integrator like ADT or perhaps a retailer like Best Buy Health. For a monthly fee, these companies could offer robot-as-a-service (RaaS) that might include user training, maintenance, insurance, and upgrades all at a predictable monthly cost.
The concept of RaaS isn’t as far-fetched as it might seem. It is already used in industrial robotics. The automobile industry provides one approach for the consumer market. Volvo, for example, introduced a subscription plan alternative to traditional car ownership or leasing. These plans often include insurance and maintenance, flexibility to change vehicles, and convenience that could translate to home robotics.
Who Will Pay for Your Robot?
There are likely to be multiple paths to paying for your new robot. Here are five.
1. Personal Purchase: AI Automation The New Luxury
Purchasing a personal robot is likely to become the next luxury buy, similar to buying a new car. Overtime, as prices decrease, it may become the new standard home appliance. Initial cost projections offered by Tesla begin around $30,000 while others suggest that a home robot will surpass $100,000, depending on functions and accessories. Future robot owners will also have to account for the initial purchase and ongoing expenses like maintenance, software updates, and insurance.
2. Robotics: High-Tech Hands Of Adult Children
Adult children might buy a robot for their aging parents. For the sandwich generation—those caught between raising children and caring for aging parents—robotic assistants could offer a much-needed helping hand. By investing in AI at home family caregivers could help ensure their parents' well-being while managing their own demanding schedules, balancing children, careers, and caregiving.
3. Caring Companies: Employer-Sponsored Robotic Care
As companies struggle with the impact of employee caregiving on productivity, innovative benefits packages are emerging. Many firms already provide subsidies for childcare and pet care. Forward-thinking firms might someday offer subsidies or subscription plans for home robots in the homes of employees' parents, recognizing the potential to improve work-life balance and reduce absenteeism among employees with caregiving responsibilities.
4. Insurance-Provided AI Helpers
Life, health, and disability insurers may see home robots as a way to reduce risk and claims. If data eventually show that home robot assistance lowers home accident rates and improves health outcomes for older adults, insurance companies might subsidize or directly provide these high-tech helpers to their policyholders. Moreover, an insurance-branded robot in the home would be a daily reminder of your insurance company’s role in your daily life, not just when you pay premiums or make a claim.
5. A Government-Issued Robot
As the population ages, governments might view robotic assistants as a cost-effective solution to growing healthcare and social service demands. Public programs could be created to finance or provide robots to achieve broader social benefits.
Planning and Paying for a Tech-Enabled Retirement
For most people, the idea of AI humanoid robots in the home is little more than the stuff of science fiction. Overtime science fiction has a way of becoming fact. Technology and global aging are converging, greatly increasing the likelihood that robots will play a significant role in our lives – particularly in older age. Much like planning and paying for where we live, our transportation, and access to healthcare, retirement planning will evolve to include the financial impacts of integrating novel technologies, including robots, into our lives. Whether through direct purchase, subscription, insurance benefit, or corporate and government initiatives, the question of who will pay for these innovations is critical to moving these ideas from the laboratory into our lives.

title: The Extreme Cost Of Training AI Models
text:
The cost of training AI models has exploded in just the past year, according to data released by the research firm Epoch AI. This development aptly shows how much more complex and capable AI models have gotten in a short time span. 2023 saw the release of the latest ChatGPT version in March by OpenAI, which kickstarted the global AI hype. Google followed suit with its advanced AI model, Gemini, in December.
Both systems have been much more expensive to train than previous AI models and their development has potentially cost hundreds of millions of dollars, according to the Epoch AI release.
